Title: PM: Govt debt rises due to budget deficit, not new spending
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has denied claims that the government is taking on new debt to finance its expenditure.
Instead, he said the country's total debt would continue to rise as long as the federal budget remained in deficit and was financed through borrowing.
Anwar, who is also finance minister, said government debt was cumulative, with each year's net borrowing adding to the outstanding debt from previous years.
"The Madani government took over the administration with existing debt exceeding RM1 trillion.
"New borrowing under the Madani government is used to finance national development, including schools, hospitals, roads, and water and electricity supplies.
"We also have to fulfil inherited financial obligations. In 2023 alone, RM13 billion was needed to settle 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB) bonds," he told the Dewan Rakyat during Prime Minister's Question Time today.
He was responding to Lee Chuan How (PH-Ipoh Timor), who asked why the government had yet to reduce national debt to a more sustainable level and whether its fiscal position allowed it to intervene to protect the economy and public welfare should the conflict in the Middle East worsen.
Anwar said annual new borrowing had declined from RM100 billion in 2022 to RM92.6 billion in 2023, RM76.8 billion in 2024 and RM75.6 billion in 2025.
He said the sharp increase in government debt between 2020 and 2022 was largely due to the Covid-19 pandemic, which required additional spending on healthcare, public assistance and economic stimulus packages.
Anwar also rejected comparisons suggesting that previous administrations had maintained significantly lower debt levels.
He said some government expenditure before 2018 had been financed through off-balance-sheet arrangements, including government guarantees and public-private partnerships, which were not fully reflected in direct federal debt figures.
The broader debt and liabilities-to-gross domestic product (GDP) ratio stood at 80.3 per cent at the end of 2017, compared with 80.9 per cent at the end of 2022 and 80.7 per cent in June 2026.
Meanwhile, the federal debt-to-GDP ratio is projected to decline from 64 per cent this year to 63 per cent in 2027.
The fiscal deficit is also expected to narrow to 3.3 per cent of GDP in 2027, compared with 6.4 per cent in 2021.
"The deficit has been declining consistently," he said.
He said fiscal consolidation would not come at the expense of public welfare, with the 2027 Budget continuing to provide assistance and subsidies to cushion Malaysians against economic uncertainties.
These include RM16 billion for Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (Sara), RM18 billion for civil service salary increases and more than RM40 billion in subsidy commitments.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Saifuddin to propose declassifying Najib's pardon minutes at cabinet meeting
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail will propose that the minutes of the Federal Territories Pardons Board meeting on Datuk Seri Najib Razak's conditional pardon be declassified at tomorrow's cabinet meeting.
He said the proposal by Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman (Muda-Muar) was a good one, as it would allow the public to gain a more comprehensive understanding of the procedures surrounding the conditional pardon granted to the former prime minister.
Saifuddin said the government also had a moral responsibility to provide clarity on questions surrounding the implementation of the pardon order.
"This is a good idea, and I can bring Muar's proposal for the Pardons Board minutes to be declassified to provide a more accurate perspective on its implementation.
"Tomorrow, there will be a cabinet meeting, and I will bring forward Muar's proposal," he said during the oral question-and-answer session in the Dewan Rakyat today.
He was responding to Syed Saddiq's supplementary question on whether the government was prepared to declassify the minutes of the Federal Territories Pardons Board meeting concerning Najib's conditional pardon.

Title: Najib sought approval for second house under house arrest, says Saifuddin
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Datuk Seri Najib Razak had submitted a written request to be allowed to use a second residence while serving the remainder of his sentence under house arrest.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the request could not be accommodated yet as the Pardons Board had expressly designated No. 11, Jalan Langgak Duta, as Najib's residence under the conditional pardon order.
Responding to a supplementary question from Suhaizan Kaiat (PH-Pulai) in the Dewan Rakyat, Saifuddin said the conditions governing Najib's house arrest came from three sources.
The first set was stipulated by the Pardons Board in its decision granting Najib a conditional pardon in the form of house arrest.
The second comprised additional conditions formulated by the Prisons Department for supervision and monitoring, including the necessary instructions and procedures under the Prisons Act.
The third involved requests made by Najib himself, including his written application to be allowed to use another house.
"At present, we are bound by the Pardons Board's decision, which specifies only one residence. Therefore, we are unable to accommodate Datuk Seri Najib's request to include another house under the additional conditions," he said.

Title: Nvidia shares plunge following reports CEO Huang could be ousted
Article:
NEW YORK: Nvidia shares plunged on Wednesday following media reports that the US chipmaker's board was considering removing chief executive Jensen Huang, reported German news agency dpa.
On Sunday, Nvidia said it had launched an investigation into reports that Huang had become the target of "foreign intelligence efforts."
There had been media reports suggesting that Huang had been having an affair with a woman whom US security circles believed had been recruited by the Chinese secret service.
Huang confirmed in an email to Nvidia staff that he had been having an affair.
The Wall Street Journal, citing unnamed sources, reported that the Nvidia board could meet shortly to decide on Huang's future. The New York Times also reported on Wednesday that Huang allegedly had another affair with a staff member who reported to him. According to the report, Huang and Nvidia initially declined to comment.
Shares of the chipmaker fell by as much as 9 per cent in after-hours trading, their lowest level since mid-2025.
Nvidia is a key player in the artificial intelligence (AI) boom. Chips from the Santa Clara-based company in Silicon Valley dominate data centres when it comes to training and operating AI.
Huang has made a name for himself as the face of the AI revolution - at company conferences and other public appearances, he tirelessly extols the world-changing role of AI in all areas of life.

Title: SP Setia earnings forecasts cut after results miss expectations
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Research houses have cut their earnings forecasts for SP Setia Bhd after its third quarter (Q3) and nine-month results missed expectations.
Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) dropped its earnings forecast for the property developer by 13.9 per cent, 11.6 per cent and 10.2 per cent for financial year 2026 (FY26), FY27 and FY28, respectively, to factor in lower sales assumptions.
The firm said SP Setia's core earnings for the cumulative nine-month period ended Sept 30, 2026, of RM75.9 million only accounted for 28.3 per cent of its full-year forecast and 21.7 per cent of consensus.
"The negative deviation in Q3 was due to lower-than-expected progress billings, mainly from its Setia Alaman project."
The company posted a core loss of RM2.2 million in the quarter under review.
"For Q4, earnings should benefit from the recognition of the land sale to another property developer and stronger billings from Setia Alaman's industrial plots."
The firm added SP Setia's historical average quarterly property sales run rate of above RM1 billion and gross profit margins rank among the strongest across peers.
However, high fixed costs, finance costs and its share of BPS losses constrain earnings conversion.
"This, in our view, sets a high sales hurdle for profitability and leaves earnings particularly vulnerable to any slowdown in sales."
HLIB kept its "Hold" call on the stock with a lower target price of 62 sen.
In a separate note, Public Investment Bank Bhd said SP Setia's results only met 39.4 per cent of its estimate and 40 per cent of the consensus.
"As such, we revised our FY26 and FY27 earnings forecast downwards by about 26 per cent to 38 per cent after adjusting our billings and margins assumptions," it said.
Separately, the firm said pre-sales remained resilient despite softer market demand, reaching RM2.34 billion for the nine-month period, supported by domestic developments of RM1.79 billion and international developments of RM431 million or about 51 per cent of its FY26 sales target of RM4.6 billion.
"We understand that it could seal two to three land sale deals to data centre players by the end of 2026 that could bump its pre-sales by year-end."
The firm kept its "Neutral" call in the stock with a lower target price of 70 sen.

Title: Japan's Mimura says markets shouldn't forget intervention risks as yen nears 160
Article:
TOKYO: Japan's top currency diplomat Atsushi Mimura on Thursday warned market participants that it's "too early to forget" this summer's intervention as the yen again edged towards the key 160-per-dollar level.
In his first remarks on foreign exchange since late September, Mimura said he believed that recent currency moves have been excessively rapid.
"It's still too early to forget what happened this summer," he added, referring to Japan's yen-buying interventions in late July through early August, including one conducted jointly with the US.
The dollar rose to 159.94 against the Japanese yen early Thursday morning, hitting its strongest in over two months, buoyed by growing expectations that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates after hot US inflation data and hawkish remarks from policymakers.
The weak yen has been a headache for Japanese policymakers as import costs have surged. The yen-based import price index jumped 24.8 per cent in October from a year earlier, data showed on Thursday.
"The dollar is likely to continue rising against the yen, underpinned by the resilience of the US economy and persistently elevated inflation driven by robust investment in AI," Mizuho Securities analysts said in a report.
"If dollar breaks above 160 and the weaker yen fuels inflation, increasing the risk of a decline in support for Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's government, Tokyo could carry out unilateral intervention," the report said.

Title: Court allows 1MDB companies to use affidavit in bid to freeze Rosmah's assets
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Court of Appeal today allowed an appeal by 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB) and 10 other companies to use an affidavit by Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor's former personal shopper in their bid to freeze her assets.
A three-member bench led by Datuk Dr Alwi Abdul Wahab unanimously overturned a High Court decision barring the companies from relying on the affidavit affirmed by Singaporean Shabnam Naraindas Daswani.
The affidavit was submitted in support of their application for a Mareva injunction.
The other members of the bench were Datuk Ismail Brahim and Datuk Leonard David Shim.
The appellate court ruled that the High Court judge had erred in dismissing the companies' application for leave to file the further affidavit.
The companies are seeking to freeze Rosmah's assets over allegations that she acquired more than 12,000 luxury items, including jewellery, watches and handbags, using approximately US$346 million allegedly misappropriated from 1MDB.
Shim, who read the judgment, said the High Court had erred in finding that exceptional circumstances had to be established before the companies could introduce the affidavit.
He said the Rules of Court did not require an applicant to establish exceptional circumstances when seeking an extension of time.
"The court also found that the companies had filed their application on June 20 last year, before written submissions in the injunction proceedings were completed on July 18.
"The delay of about two-and-a-half months in preparing the affidavit had been satisfactorily explained.
"Shabnam, who was initially named as the second defendant in the lawsuit, agreed to provide her account only after the companies discontinued their claim against her through a consent order on April 9 last year.
"Her affidavit, comprising 319 pages across nine volumes, contained invoices, correspondence with luxury goods vendors, photographs and communications involving fugitive businessman Low Taek Jho, better known as Jho Low, and Eric Tan.
"The documents also included details of payments for luxury items through offshore entities, allegedly using funds misappropriated from 1MDB," he said.
The appellate court said the affidavit was relevant to the companies' claims and their applications for Mareva and proprietary injunctions.
It added that the evidence could be used to challenge Rosmah's defence that the luxury items were gifts from third parties.
The court also found that allowing the affidavit would not cause substantial prejudice to Rosmah, as she would be given sufficient time to examine its contents and respond.
It said the companies would suffer greater injustice if they were prevented from introducing evidence that could only have been obtained following the consent order with Shabnam.
The court also awarded RM30,000 in costs to the companies, subject to allocatur.
The companies were represented by a legal team comprising Datuk Lim Chee Wee, Nathalie Ker and Henna Sanghvi, while Rosmah was represented by Datuk Rajan Navaratnam and Sheena Sebastian.
In their lawsuit, the companies alleged that funds misappropriated from 1MDB had been channelled through eight offshore entities in the British Virgin Islands and Seychelles.
They claimed that the funds were subsequently used to purchase more than 12,000 luxury items from 48 vendors across at least 14 jurisdictions.
The companies are seeking a Mareva injunction involving US$346.01 million, a proprietary injunction over the luxury items and an interim preservation order pending the disposal of their lawsuit against Rosmah.

Title: Najib barred from media, political activities under house arrest
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Datuk Seri Najib Razak is prohibited from making media statements, appearing on social media platforms or participating in political activities while serving the remainder of his sentence under house arrest.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail told the Dewan Rakyat that the conditions were among several restrictions imposed under the conditional pardon order issued by the Pardons Board.
He said the conditions also included restrictions on movement, visitors and the use of telecommunications devices, as well as mandatory participation in rehabilitation and intervention programmes.
Najib must remain at No. 11, Jalan Langgak Duta, and cannot move to another residence or leave the premises without prior written permission.
He is also prohibited from receiving visitors without written approval and may only live with his immediate family members, including his wives, children, in-laws and grandchildren.

Title: GST reintroduction not a political decision - Anwar
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government's refusal to reintroduce the Goods and Services Tax (GST) is driven by macroeconomic considerations rather than political reasons, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
Anwar, who is also finance minister, said the government remained concerned that reintroducing the broad-based consumption tax would place an additional burden on Malaysians whose incomes were still relatively low.
"This is not about politics. What is political about it if it benefits the country's economy and the people?
"For me, this is an important macroeconomic consideration that is debated in many countries, not just here," he told the Dewan Rakyat.
Anwar was responding to Datuk Seri Dr Ronald Kiandee (PN-Beluran), who questioned whether the government's insistence on retaining the Sales and Service Tax (SST) was driven by political considerations rather than the merits of the taxation systems.
Kiandee argued that GST could address the cascading effect of SST, where taxes imposed at different stages of production and distribution could increase costs for businesses and consumers.
He also questioned whether the government would consider incorporating GST features into a hybrid taxation system.
Anwar said the tax could be reconsidered when Malaysians' incomes had increased substantially, citing RM4,000 to RM5,000 as an illustrative level.
"The people's incomes are still relatively low. We are only trying to raise the minimum wage to RM2,000, and even that is difficult because many businesses are opposed to it.
"That is why I reject the proposal to introduce GST at this time," he said.
Anwar also challenged claims that GST would necessarily generate significantly higher government revenue.
He said SST currently contributed 2.2 per cent of gross domestic product (GDP), matching the contribution recorded under GST in 2017.
"SST now generates 2.2 per cent of GDP. That is the same figure as GST in 2017.
"So there is no basis to claim that introducing GST would increase revenue," he said.
He added that about 700,000 businesses were affected by GST in 2018, compared with 130,000 under SST this year.
Anwar acknowledged that GST had advantages in terms of efficiency and transparency, but said those benefits had to be weighed against its potential impact on lower-income households.
He also said major business groups and chambers of commerce had repeatedly called for GST to be reintroduced during Budget consultations.
However, he maintained that the government's priority was to ensure the taxation system did not worsen the cost-of-living pressures faced by ordinary Malaysians.
Anwar said he remained open to examining proposals supporting GST and welcomed further debate on the merits of both taxation systems.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Najib allowed to live only with immediate family under house arrest
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Datuk Seri Najib Razak is only allowed to live with his immediate family members while serving the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the conditions stipulated by the Pardons Board allowed Najib to live with his wives, children, sons- and daughters-in-law, and grandchildren.
In the Dewan rakyat, he said, anyone else would require prior written approval from the board.
Najib is also prohibited from receiving visitors without written permission.
Other conditions include restrictions on his movement, telephone use and media appearances, as well as a ban on participating in political activities.

Title: Man arrested hours after stealing wallet from car in Cheras
Article:
KAJANG: A man in his 20s was arrested after he was caught on closed-circuit television (CCTV) stealing a wallet from a car parked at a house in Taman Rakan, Cheras, yesterday.
Kajang police chief, Assistant Commissioner Naazron Abdul Yusof, said the theft was discovered by the 28-year-old victim at 8am when he realised that his wallet, which he had left inside his vehicle, was missing.
He said a review of CCTV footage showed an unidentified man entering the compound of the victim's house before taking the wallet, which contained his identity card, ATM card and debit card.
The footage showed the man, dressed in dark clothing, moving around the porch, where several motorcycles and a car were parked.
He was then seen approaching the vehicle before moving towards the entrance of the house and leaving the porch.
Naazron said the victim lodged a police report at 10.15am yesterday.
"Acting on information and intelligence gathered, a team from the Kajang district police headquarters' Criminal Investigation Division arrested a local man in his 20s in Taman Rakan, Cheras, at 10pm the same day.
"Police also seized a Modenas Kriss motorcycle and a black helmet believed to be linked to the case," he said in a statement today.
Naazron said the suspect was brought before the Kajang magistrate's court today, where a one-day remand order was granted to facilitate further investigations.
The case is being investigated under Section 379 of the Penal Code for theft, which carries a maximum jail term of seven years, a fine or both upon conviction.
Those with information about the incident are urged to contact investigating officer Sergeant Mohamad Zamri Mohamad Nor at 010-2848761.

Title: Govt studies extending i-Sayang scheme to foreign wives
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government, through the Employees Provident Fund (EPF), will continue to study a proposal to expand the scope and coverage of the EPF i-Sayang scheme to allow Malaysian husbands to make voluntary contributions for their non-citizen wives.
The Finance Ministry (MOF) said the proposal would be studied carefully, taking into account the importance of protecting families' retirement savings and ensuring the programme's sustainability.
"The government takes note of the proposal to expand the eligibility criteria for i-Sayang recipients to allow non-citizen wives to receive transferred contributions from their Malaysian citizen husbands.
The proposal requires careful consideration to ensure that any expansion remains aligned with the original objectives of i-Sayang and the EPF's retirement savings policy framework.
"In this regard, the suitability of its implementation must be carefully assessed, including its implications for retirement savings protection and objectives, as well as legal, governance, operational and programme sustainability aspects, before further consideration is given," the ministry said in a written parliamentary reply published on Parliament's website today.
i-Sayang is a government initiative that allows husbands to voluntarily transfer two per cent of their employee contributions to their wives' EPF accounts.
Since its introduction in March 2023, a total of 233,371 husbands nationwide have registered as contributors, involving 233,547 wives as recipients.
As at Aug 31, 2026, a total of RM563.6 million had been transferred through i-Sayang.

Title: Minimum wage hike should push businesses to improve productivity
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's latest minimum wage increase is expected to benefit workers through better incomes, while encouraging businesses to step up efforts to improve productivity to ensure that higher wages can be sustained without putting further pressure on prices.
CGS International Securities Malaysia chief economist Nazmi Idrus said wage growth had helped workers recover some of the purchasing power lost during the high-inflation period following the Covid-19 pandemic.
He said wages had gradually caught up with inflation, although any fresh increase in prices could erode some of the gains made by households.
"During periods of high inflation post-pandemic, we saw the erosion of spending power. That has recovered somewhat as wages have clawed back above inflation, but potentially higher inflation could erode those gains," he told Bernama.
On the government's Progressive Wage Policy, Nazmi described it as a good initiative, although its reach remained limited, with only about 50,000 workers currently involved.
He said the programme should be expanded to benefit more workers and help ensure that wage growth was supported by productivity improvements.
According to Bank Negara Malaysia's Annual Report 2025, despite moderate inflation, many households continue to grapple with higher living costs amid slow wage growth. To secure better living standards and strengthen purchasing power, income growth needs to outpace price increases.
The report said that when expenses rise faster than incomes, even small price increases can have a significant impact on households, influencing perceptions of affordability and how they view the broader economy.
Recent income measures, such as revisions to the minimum wage, have helped ease the burden on more than five million workers in Malaysia. Over the longer term, however, deeper structural reforms are needed to address the root causes of subdued wage growth in the country, Bank Negara said.
Meanwhile, Small and Medium Enterprises Association of Malaysia (Samenta) national president Datuk William Ng said the exemption granted to SMEs from the latest minimum wage increase would give smaller businesses some room to manage their costs, particularly those operating in towns with lower living costs.
He said the direct impact on SMEs in major urban centres such as the Klang Valley, Johor Bahru and Penang was expected to be limited, as many were already paying wages above RM2,000.
"What the exemption means is that for SMEs in smaller towns where the cost of living is lower, they are not forced to raise wages at a time when we are facing severe margin compression.
"At the same time, it allows and encourages SMEs in the main urban centres to pay more at their own pace," he said.
He urged SMEs to use the opportunity to step up automation and digitalisation to improve productivity and reduce their reliance on workers.
"Regardless of the exemption this round, we must realise that wages will go up, whether driven by regulation or by market forces, and as such, increasing productivity is the only way forward," he said.
Echoing this view, Malaysia Semiconductor Industry Association president Datuk Seri Wong Siew Hai said the need to improve productivity was not limited to SMEs, as large companies also had to find ways to manage rising costs while maintaining their competitiveness both in Malaysia and globally.
He said businesses should consider adopting automation and artificial intelligence, as well as improving product quality and operational efficiency, to reduce costs and remain competitive.
"Also, companies need to take care of the salary compression issue for other levels. So, overall costs will increase," he added.
In the 2027 Budget announcement, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the government had agreed to raise the minimum wage to RM2,000 from RM1,700, effective June 2027, with an exemption for micro, small and medium enterprises with annual sales revenue below RM50 million.
He also said the government would reform the worker income framework by introducing a minimum wage of RM2,500 per month for semi-skilled workers and graduates.
Anwar also welcomed the commitment by government-linked investment companies and government-linked companies to raise the living wage benchmark to RM3,400 from RM3,100 per month, a move expected to benefit 230,000 workers.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MyNews targets 720 outlets by Q2 FY27
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Mynews Holdings Bhd plans to open another eight stores by the end of 2026, bringing its total network to 720 outlets by the middle of the second quarter of its current financial year 2027 (Q2 FY27).
As at end-October 2026, the convenience store operator had 712 outlets, as the company prioritised profitable store expansion following the closure of 69 underperforming outlets.
The convenience store operator recorded a net addition of three stores, representing a 0.4 per cent year-on-year increase.
"Mynews remains selective in choosing new store locations, prioritising productivity over network expansion, although it remains open to higher rental locations such as airports and shopping malls where sales potential is strong," CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd said.
"Despite modest network growth, we view the improvement in store productivity positively, with average sales per store rising eight per cent year-on-year (YoY) at Mynews and five per cent YoY at CU in Q3 FY26, supported by store rationalisation and a better product mix," it said in a note.
The firm said management expects further growth from an improved product range and new launches, particularly higher-margin ready-to-eat (RTE) products such as chilled desserts and smaller-portioned meals.
Food currently accounts for 52 per cent of sales at CU stores, compared with a low teens' contribution at Mynews outlets.
However, the firm said rising rental, logistics and labour costs continue to weigh on Mynews' profitability despite improving sales momentum.
It estimated that the increase in the minimum wage to RM2,000 per month from June 2027 could raise the company's annual labour costs by RM4.3 million, assuming 40 per cent of its 3,000 employees are affected.
"To mitigate these pressures, Mynews plans selective store-level price adjustments based on local demand, alongside further cost optimisation.
"The company is also investing in artificial intelligence-driven automation, with the potential to reduce its 300 headquarters workforce by 20 to 30 per cent, having already cut finance headcount by 15 per cent," it said.
The firm said implementation costs could weigh on near-term profit margins, but these initiatives are expected to gradually reduce reliance on labour and improve inventory management, with more significant efficiency gains anticipated in FY28 and FY29.
CIMB Securities said Mynews is exploring plans to develop a new distribution centre on its recently acquired 5.46-hectare site in Serendah within the next two years.
The proposed facility would support the expansion of chilled and frozen RTE products while easing capacity constraints at its existing Sungai Buloh distribution centre and Kota Damansara production hub.
The firm said greater automation at the proposed facility could potentially halve the company's current workforce of about 170 drivers, resulting in longer-term logistics cost savings.
CIMB Securities maintained its 'Hold' call on Mynews with an unchanged target price of 51 sen, citing persistent cost pressures that could limit its near-term earnings recovery.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: CelcomDigi steps up cyber and climate safeguards
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: CelcomDigi Bhd is strengthening its cybersecurity capabilities and climate resilience measures to mitigate growing digital threats and environmental risks as it seeks to safeguard its network operations and reputation, said CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd.
The firm said the telecommunications company had stepped up customer protection efforts by flagging 260 million suspected scam calls and blocking 22 million SMS messages monthly amid rising digital scam threats.
Analysts Choong Chen Foong and Kenny Lim said CelcomDigi's multi-layered cybersecurity strategy, which includes protection at both network and device levels, would help strengthen its ability to address emerging cyber threats.
"Overall, we view CelcomDigi's initiatives under its environmental, social and governance (ESG) roadmap and the progress made thus far positively," they said.
CelcomDigi shared its progress during its Responsible Business Day on Nov 5, 2026, themed "Responsibility in the Age of AI", marking the third year of its five-year ESG strategy.
The company has also reached 18.3 million Malaysians through its SAFE Internet programme to raise awareness of online safety.
It has introduced WebShield and MobileShield to provide additional protection against digital threats, while rolling out a Responsible AI Governance Framework in 2026 to promote transparent and accountable artificial intelligence adoption across its organisation.
Choong and Lim said these initiatives were increasingly relevant as businesses and consumers faced evolving cybersecurity risks alongside wider AI adoption.
Beyond digital protection, CelcomDigi has continued to make progress on decarbonisation, reducing its Scope 1 and 2 emissions by four per cent year-on-year in 2025.
Its carbon intensity also declined 30 per cent over the financial year 2023 to 2025 to 0.04 tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent per terabyte, reflecting energy efficiency improvements across its network.
These included the deployment of energy-efficient equipment across 15,000 sites, hybrid batteries and on-site solar installations.
The company reaffirmed its 2035 climate targets of reducing Scope 1 and 2 emissions by 63 per cent and Scope 3 emissions by 66.3 per cent, as it works towards its net-zero ambition by 2050.
It is also incorporating physical climate risks into network planning to protect its telecommunications infrastructure against extreme weather events.
The analysts said CelcomDigi had implemented tower plinth elevation and structural reinforcement at 200 sites to mitigate potential flood and storm damage.
The company has also undertaken climate risk assessments and introduced AI-driven weather forecasting in high-risk areas to strengthen infrastructure resilience.
Choong and Lim said such measures could help minimise service disruptions and potential financial losses arising from infrastructure damage, reputational harm and regulatory penalties.
"We believe its proactive measures to address cybersecurity threats and physical climate risks should help maintain its network resilience, minimise service disruptions and mitigate potential financial losses from reputational damage, regulatory fines and infrastructure damage repairs," they said.
CIMB Securities maintained its "Buy" call on CelcomDigi with an unchanged target price of RM3.65.
The firm also retained its financial year 2026 to 2028 core earnings per share forecasts, citing the company's progress in managing ESG-related risks.
However, it identified higher-than-expected costs and adverse regulatory developments as key downside risks to its outlook.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: General strike over housing brings out hundreds of thousands in Spain
Article:
MADRID: Hundreds of thousands of protesters marched across Spain on Wednesday during a general strike over housing affordability and purchasing power just weeks before an early general election.
Unions reported a significant response in some sectors in Spain's first nationwide 24-hour stoppage since 2012, but business leaders played down the participation.
Braving pouring rain, some 120,000 demonstrators marched through central Madrid carrying placards shaped like houses and chanting, "We have no home," as they called for more affordable housing, according to an estimate by the authorities.
"People work a lot and it isn't enough to pay the rent, to pay for a house," Paula Diaz, a 25-year-old theatre technician who lives with her parents, told AFP at the Madrid protest.
"I hope a government that benefits us comes to power, especially the working class," she added, referring to the November 29 election.
In Barcelona, where the authorities estimated 55,000 people marched through the city's luxury Passeig de Gracia commercial thoroughfare, Maria Pinana told AFP, "The law of supply and demand does not apply to housing."
"The price of rents should be regulated," said the 34-year-old microbiologist, who lives with friends in a flat where parts of the ceiling have collapsed.
Tens of thousands more attended protests held in other cities across Spain.
The size of the demonstrations was seen as an indicator of public discontent before the snap election, where the right-wing opposition is predicted to defeat Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez.
Clashes broke out after rallies in Barcelona and Madrid, as groups of hooded and masked protesters hurled projectiles at police and set rubbish bins on fire.
Police used rubber bullet launchers and tear gas to disperse the small groups. Eighteen people were arrested in Barcelona.
- 'Failure' -
In Madrid, where many shops opened as normal, demonstrators earlier on Wednesday blocked some roads, a picket action that was replicated across the country.
Public transport suffered disruption even with the implementation of minimum service requirements for commuter trains, metros and buses, especially in and around Barcelona.
In contrast, Madrid's metro said 93 per cent of its trains ran in the early morning, although passenger numbers were down by around half.
UGT union leader Pepe Alvarez told public broadcaster RTVE that the participation was "massive", with a "total" stoppage in some regions making the strike "a huge success."
But his union acknowledged participation was "uneven", with large mobilisation in the car manufacturing, petrochemicals and meat sectors and in coastal regions.
The CEOE organisation, which represents business leaders, called the strike "a failure", adding in a statement that activity had gone ahead normally in most sectors.
Electricity demand had fallen by around five per cent, "significantly lower" than in previous strikes, the CEOE said.
- 'New cycle' -
The main UGT and CCOO unions called the strike following a wave of nationwide protests over access to housing, sparked by the eviction in September of an 87-year-old Madrid pensioner.
Valeria Racu, spokeswoman for the Madrid Tenants' Union, which has been at the forefront of protests for weeks, vowed to "put an end to the housing business in this country."
"A new cycle is beginning with trade unionism and conflict at its centre. This day of strikes has been a resounding success," she said.
Sanchez called the election, initially scheduled for 2027, after his minority government failed to secure parliamentary approval for a package of housing measures proposed in response to the demonstrations.
Business groups and the right have rejected the strike, seeing it as an election-related gambit rather than a genuine labour dispute.
But the unions have insisted the strike is directed against all levels of the state and not only the right, which voted down the government's housing decrees.
They have defended the walkout as an exceptional measure intended to generate broad social pressure for action on soaring housing costs.
Isabel Iglesias, a nurse who lives in Madrid, said housing was the issue "that is affecting me the most." She pays a rent of 1,000 euros (US$1,100) with her partner but earns just 1,700 euros a month.
Iglesias, 27, said Sanchez, who has been in power since 2018, "could have done much more" on housing, urging the next government "to listen to everyone and get their act together."

Title: UK house sales outlook is darkest since 2023
Article:
LONDON: British property surveyors were the most downbeat about the short-term outlook for house sales in more than three years in October, as rising interest rates for mortgages compressed demand, a survey showed on Thursday.
The Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors said its outlook for house sales over the 12 months fell to -17 in October, with surveyors expecting the broadest drop in sales since July 2023.
"Home buyer demand remains subdued, and respondents are bracing for a weaker year ahead for sales given the persistent macroeconomic challenges being faced," RICS head of market research Tarrant Parsons said.
RICS' headline house price balance dropped to -36 last month from September's downwardly revised reading of -34, and a slightly bigger drop than the -34 forecast in a Reuters poll of economists.
Its gauge of new buyer enquiries held at -24, while agreed sales fell to -24 from -18, the weakest in three months.
In rentals, tenant demand strengthened, and landlords reduced properties put on the market.
Expectations for growth in rents over the next three months climbed to +41, from +29, its strongest since early 2024.
The Bank of England raised interest rates to 4.0 per cent from 3.75 per cent last week, its first hike in three years
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Beyond Buildings: BCB's vision for Malaysia's property landscape
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's property industry is entering a new phase, with developers facing growing expectations to deliver quality developments that balance lifestyle needs, commercial viability and environmental sustainability.
For BCB Bhd executive director Tan Lindy, the future of property development lies not just in delivering projects, but in creating communities that offer lasting value.
She believes developers must look beyond immediate market opportunities and adopt a longer-term perspective, taking into account changing consumer preferences, evolving lifestyles and the growing importance of sustainable communities.
At BCB, Tan is steering the group's property development direction while contributing to the wider real estate industry through her involvement in professional organisations.
Established in 1988, BCB has grown from its roots in Kluang, Johor, into a diversified property developer with interests spanning residential townships, high-end residential projects, commercial developments and property-related investments.
Listed on the Main Market of Bursa Malaysia in 1996, the group has expanded its footprint across Batu Pahat, Johor Baru and the Klang Valley.
In a statement, BCB said it continues to pursue township and mixed-development opportunities in Johor, reinforcing its presence in the state where its property development journey began.
As executive director, Tan oversees BCB's property development projects and subsidiary companies, contributing to the group's business strategies and development initiatives.
In the financial year ended June 30, 2026 (FY26), BCB recorded a revenue of RM351.2 million compared with RM208.39 million achieved in FY 25. Pre-tax profit rose to RM44.34 million from RM15.95 million.
According to BCB's Annual Report 2026, it remains cautiously optimistic about the prospects of the property market and will continue to focus on the execution of its ongoing developments.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Electricity bill protection expansion to cost RM248mil over 4 months
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Expanding electricity bill protection to households consuming up to 800 kWh a month is expected to cost RM248 million over four months, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof said.
Fadillah, who is also Energy Transition and Water Transformation minister, said the measure would benefit about 90 per cent, or eight million, of domestic consumers in Peninsular Malaysia.
He said the financial implications comprised three main components.
"The RM180 million Automatic Fuel Adjustment (AFA) cost will be jointly borne by the government and Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) for September, while TNB will fully absorb the remaining costs from October to December.
"TNB will also fully bear the RM36 million retail charge for the period from September to December, while the government will absorb the RM32 million in Sales and Service Tax exemptions for the same period," he said in a written parliamentary reply yesterday.
He was responding to Lim Guan Eng (PH-Bagan), who asked about the cost of electricity bill protection for domestic consumers under the existing 600 kWh monthly threshold, equivalent to about RM220, and the proposed expansion to 800 kWh.
Lim also asked who would bear the costs and whether the threshold could be raised to 1,000 kWh, equivalent to about RM367 a month, following increased electricity consumption due to hot weather and haze.
On the proposal to raise the threshold to 1,000 kWh a month, Fadillah said he welcomed suggestions for improvements, but stressed that the proposal needed to be examined thoroughly.
He said the assessment would take into account the financial implications, the number of consumers who would benefit, the funding source and the measure's effectiveness in helping households affected by higher electricity consumption.
Meanwhile, Fadillah said the ministry, together with the Energy Commission, TNB and the Single Buyer, was reviewing the AFA mechanism to identify improvements for implementation from 2027.
"The review takes into account consumption patterns and levels by consumer category, changes in fuel and generation costs, and the impact on domestic and non-domestic bills.
"A fairer and more targeted approach to cost distribution, including the causer-pays principle, is also being evaluated to ensure additional generation costs are shared more equitably," he said.
He said the government was also considering consumers' affordability, the industrial sector's competitiveness and the financial sustainability of the electricity supply industry.
Any decision on extending the protection would be made only after the review was completed, he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Govt spent RM70mil to host Bahrain F1 Grand Prix
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government spent RM70 million to host the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) last month.
Youth and Sports Minister Dr Mohammed Taufiq Johari said the sum covered circuit maintenance and SIC's operating costs, while Bahrain bore the remaining expenses.
He said hosting the race in Malaysia was estimated to cost RM350 million, including the rights fee and SIC's preparations.
"Based on information from Formula One Management, the event generated an economic impact of almost RM950 million for the country.
"This covers the hospitality, tourism, international aviation, transport, goods and services, food and beverage, and circuit operations sectors, as well as the Litar Rasa Madani programme," he said in a written parliamentary reply yesterday.
He said detailed figures would be provided in an economic impact study report being prepared by a consultancy firm appointed by SIC.
The event also created about 7,300 jobs, he said.
These comprised 6,167 jobs in businesses and services catering to visitors, 757 in race operations and infrastructure, and 376 involving racing teams, sponsors and F1 operations.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Trump to flex muscles on Asia tour after midterms losses
Article:
WASHINGTON: After his party suffered a midterms hammering, President Donald Trump faces a new challenge: proving he is still the boss of US foreign policy on the global stage.
With Trump politically hamstrung as he enters the remaining two-year "lame duck" period of his White House tenure, world leaders may be quietly wondering how to leverage the new balance of power in Washington.
The 80-year-old Republican heads to the Asean summit in the Philippines and APEC summit in China against a radically transformed and hostile political landscape at home, after the Democrats seized control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate.
Constitutionally barred from seeking a third term in the 2028 presidential race, the unpredictable billionaire could be all the more inclined to focus his energy on the international stage.
"After bad midterms, this is how presidents reset," Edgard Kagan, an expert at the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS), told a news briefing.
Iran, trade, China
That is especially true for Trump on his Asian tour, where he is unlikely to be pressed publicly on domestic politics.
China has described the midterms as an "internal affair" and said it is "willing to continue working" with the US after Republicans lost control of both chambers of Congress.
But the power shift in Washington will still be on leaders' radars, said Joshua Kurlantzick, an expert in Southeast Asia and South Asia at the Council on Foreign Relations.
"In private, many (Asian) leaders are relieved," Kurlantzick wrote in an article this month.
"The Iran war has been particularly challenging for the United States' Asian partners and allies, and they hope that after the midterm results US President Donald Trump's decision-making on the issue will become more predictable."
Trump has said several times since the midterms that renewed fighting between the US and Iran is unlikely.
A Democratic-controlled Congress could also take a tougher stance towards China, Kurlantzick added, backtracking on the Trump administration's "soft approach" to Beijing that has sparked unease among US allies in Asia.
Leaders in the world's largest continent are also hoping to see Democrats push back against Trump's barrage of tariffs on trading partners, which have hit Asian economies heavily reliant on exports.
Democratic House leader Hakeem Jeffries has urged Congress to reassert its authority over US trade policy.
The Democrats will not have an easy time undoing Trump's policies, though.
The president enjoys broad authority over trade and holds veto power over congressional legislation — which he has vowed to use.
[[nid:1575929]]
High-profile meeting
Trump relishes dramatic gestures, and foreign policy provides an ideal arena for high-profile meetings, such as those with Chinese and Russian leaders Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin.
Trump told reporters this week that he expected to meet Xi and Putin at the Apec summit in Shenzhen, China, scheduled for Nov 18-19.
The president said "denuclearisation" and ending the war in Iran would be on the agenda.
But the bigger goal for Trump may well be a single photograph of himself standing with the two other leaders he views as his great-power equals, said Kurt Campbell, chair of The Asia Group and a senior diplomat during the Biden administration.
"I think in many respects this could be 'the meeting is the message'," Campbell said.
Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, who watched in horror as the White House appeared to pivot towards Moscow this year, has warned against a "Yalta 2.0", referring to Western leaders dividing Europe with the Soviet Union in 1945.
Victor Cha, president of geopolitics and foreign policy and Korea chair at CSIS, said the Republicans' midterm defeat made a high-profile meeting all the more likely.
"One that he (Trump) has personally staked a lot of time over two terms has been on North Korea," Cha said.
"There's nobody else in the US government that makes policy on North Korea except the president, so I think that he'll be focused on that sort of legacy issue."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Straight Path Convention returns for 13th edition with focus on influence
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR:
The Straight Path Convention (TSP) returns for its 13th edition on Nov 14 and 15, focusing on how influence can strengthen Muslim identity and shape society.
The annual English-language Islamic educational convention will be held at the Grand Banquet Hall, UTM Hotel & Residence, Kuala Lumpur, under the theme "INFLUENCE: Impact That Shapes Your Legacy".
The two-day event aims to explore how people can use their influence, regardless of their background or position, to promote positive values and contribute to society.
TSP co-founders and directors Haji Ariff and Encik Farid said influence should not be measured by popularity, social media following or position, but by the positive changes people bring to the lives of others.
"Every individual has influence, whether they realise it or not. However, true influence is not measured by the number of followers, popularity or one's position, but by the goodness one spreads and the positive changes one brings into the lives of others," they said.
FIVE SPEAKERS FROM FIVE COUNTRIES
This year's convention will feature five speakers from five countries: Dr Ali Albarghouthi (Canada), Dr Muhammad Salah (Egypt), Dr Abu Hafiz Salleh Hudin (Malaysia), Sheikh Hisham Abu Yusuf (United Kingdom) and Sheikh Wael Ibrahim (Australia).
The speakers will lead sessions exploring various aspects of influence in personal and societal life, covering topics such as "The Silent Influencer", "Beyond the Screen, Home: Where Influence Begins", "Flipping the Narrative: Islamophobia" and "The Price of Fame".
The convention will conclude with a session titled "Be the Influence", encouraging participants to apply what they have learnt through meaningful action.
CONVENTION EXPANDS REACH
For the first time, TSP will also be broadcast live on Tonton, allowing those unable to attend in person to follow the sessions online.
The organisers said this year's theme reflected the need for Muslims to understand how influence, particularly through social media, could shape people's thoughts and behaviour.
They said the convention would also examine how influence could be channelled responsibly through Islamic principles.
The organisers hope the event will offer fresh perspectives and encourage participants to become agents of positive change in their communities.
The convention will be held at the Grand Banquet Hall, UTM Hotel & Residence, Kuala Lumpur.
For more information and ticket purchases, visit
TSP's official website
. The live broadcast will be available on Tonton.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka polls: Lok puts community service at heart of Bandar Hilir campaign
Article:
MELAKA: Unfazed by a three-cornered contest in an opposition stronghold, BN's Bandar Hilir candidate Jasmine Lok is banking on her years of grassroots service to win voters' support.
The MCA candidate, who has served as a Melaka Historic City Council (MBMB) councillor since 2022, said her experience in community work had given her the confidence to serve the constituency.
"I am not afraid. We live in a democracy, and I do not make predictions about who has more support. My confidence comes from working on the ground since 2011," said Lok.
"I started as a personal assistant to a city councillor, worked as a personal assistant to a member of parliament, and was later appointed as a councillor myself.
"I have the experience and understand how the government works," she added.
Lok faces a tough challenge in Bandar Hilir, traditionally a DAP stronghold, where she is up against PH's Leng Chau Yen and a candidate from Bersama.
Rather than dwelling on past election results, Lok said her main focus was on resolving everyday problems faced by local residents and small traders.
One of her key pledges is the 'Jasmine Care Van', a free transport service to take elderly residents living in older walk-up flats to hospitals and clinics for regular check-ups.
"Many senior citizens suffer from illnesses such as diabetes and have difficulty walking, especially those living on upper floors without lifts.
"Under this plan, youth volunteers will accompany them, wait with them at the hospital, and bring them safely home," she said.
She also wants to establish a weekend community centre to keep senior citizens active and bring younger and older residents together.
To revive vacant shop lots and boost the local economy, Lok proposed setting up affordable start-up spaces and weekend bazaars for young entrepreneurs.
She said the initiative would help promote Melaka's heritage by showcasing unique artisan products instead of the common souvenirs sold to tourists.
On traffic congestion and the proposed Car-Free Zone in the Unesco heritage area, Lok said a balanced approach was needed.
"Car-free zones are common in heritage sites overseas, but I understand that any new plan must not hurt local residents and traders. We cannot push for progress while ignoring the daily struggles of the community.
"My idea is to build multi-storey car parks outside the main area and use buggy shuttles to bring visitors into the heritage zone," she said.
She added that close cooperation between MBMB, the police and local residents was key to addressing traffic congestion.
MCA is fielding candidates in four seats under the BN banner in the Melaka election. It is defending Machap Jaya and Klebang while seeking to wrest the opposition strongholds of Bandar Hilir and Kota Laksamana.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Record crowd greets Pope Leo as he calls Peru his homeland in emotional visit
Article:
LIMA: Pope Leo was greeted by the largest crowd of his papacy in an emotional return to Peru on Wednesday, declaring the South American country where he served as a missionary for two decades his homeland.
The huge crowds, estimated at 3 million by local officials, pressed against police and security barriers, waving balloons and flags and chanting "Leo, Leo, Leo". The pope was all smiles as he toured in an open-air popemobile and waved energetically on the final leg of his three-country, 12-day trip.
In a closely watched speech to President Keiko Fujimori shortly after being greeted in Lima, the first Peruvian citizen to lead the Catholic Church urged the president to build confidence among her people after her narrow election victory earlier this year, and alluded to the contested legacy of her father, the late former president Alberto Fujimori.
"This return visit holds a very special meaning for me," the pope said at Lima's Gran Teatro Nacional, mentioning the many friendships he had made during his 20 years in the country and his love for a national dish, ceviche.
"Today I understand how much of this land remains with me and how much of my own story also belongs to you," he said. "I can tell you, with deep gratitude, that I am returning to my homeland."
Poignant scenes as pope returns home
Leo, originally from Chicago, is visiting Peru on the final and most personal stop of the most intense overseas trip by a pope in decades, after touring Uruguay and Argentina.
The six-day visit is expected to include poignant scenes as the pope sees old friends and spends three days in the northern city of Chiclayo, where he was bishop from 2015 to 2023.
Crowds lined the streets of the capital for miles to welcome Leo, evoking images of previous papal trips to Catholic strongholds such as the Philippines, Mexico and Brazil. The main plaza in Lima, filled with people waving flags and wearing pope-themed shirts, erupted into loud cheers as a big screen showed Leo's plane touching down.
Camila Cerazo, 27, arrived with her toddler, husband and relatives, saying she hoped her son might someday remember the excitement surrounding Leo's arrival.
"Since people found out the pope had Peruvian nationality, they identified with him much more," she said.
Peru has prepared for the homecoming with fervour: A 14-metre statue depicting Leo with outstretched arms towers over a seaside park in Callao, while merchants in Lima are selling pope-themed shirts and souvenirs, and inmates at the country's largest women's prison have stitched velvet dolls bearing his likeness.
[[nid:1575916]]
Wading into politics
In the first of his scheduled 22 events in Peru, Leo urged Fujimori to confront the wounds of the country's turbulent past, alluding to her father's contested legacy.
Alberto Fujimori was in office from 1990 to 2000 and spent many years in jail after leaving the presidency, having been convicted of human rights abuses. He was pardoned in 2017 and died in 2024.
"Past events deserve to be treated with justice and sensitivity, leaving room for harmony to grow and for differences to be addressed with respect," Leo said.
Without referring directly to an internal conflict that lasted from around 1980 to 2000, Leo said Peru had endured "difficult times" that had tested the country.
He called on Peruvians to cultivate "honesty, integrity, and a willingness to engage with others", saying those qualities were essential to sustaining trust and democratic institutions.
In her welcome to the pope, Fujimori said his visit was an invitation for Peru to pursue its "unfinished task" of national reconciliation.
When Alberto Fujimori was pardoned in 2017, Leo, then Bishop Robert Prevost, criticised the move, saying the former president should personally seek forgiveness from victims if Peru was to achieve genuine reconciliation.
Keiko Fujimori leaned heavily on her father's political legacy during her presidential campaign, pledging uncompromising security measures to deal with rising crime.
Ahead of Leo's visit, Martin Cassinelli, an analyst at the Atlantic Council, said any call for Peru to investigate its past would be unwelcome to President Fujimori.
"If there's anything that could potentially be at odds with the current Fujimori government, it would be a reflection on the past," Cassinelli said.
Relations between the late Fujimori's government and sectors of the Catholic Church were frequently tense, particularly over human rights during the state's fight against the Maoist Shining Path insurgency. Church figures also opposed the 1995 amnesty for members of the security forces accused of rights abuses.
[[nid:1575915]]
A record-setting tour
A Vatican statement, citing local officials, said 3 million people greeted Leo on his arrival in Lima, setting another record for the biggest crowd of his papacy after an estimated 2.5 million people attended an outdoor Mass he celebrated in Buenos Aires earlier this week.
Leo ended the Argentina leg of his South American tour earlier on Wednesday with another outdoor Mass that drew a crowd of 2 million outside the shrine of Our Lady of Lujan, Argentina's most important Catholic devotional site.
The pope also visited one of Argentina's largest penitentiaries, where he hugged several inmates and urged guards to treat detainees humanely.
During his three-day visit to Argentina, Leo urged consideration for the disadvantaged at a time when the Church has criticised President Javier Milei's austerity agenda for affecting the poor.
Milei's eyes welled with tears as he bade farewell to Leo on the tarmac, a surprising display of emotion from a president known for directing insults at Leo's Argentine predecessor, Francis.
Leo began the trip less than a month after lung cancer surgery and has appeared in good form, giving long speeches in a firm, clear voice.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 211 companies deactivated from eCOSS for non-compliance
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 211 companies had their access to the Cooking Oil Price Stabilisation Scheme System (eCOSS) deactivated as of Oct 30 for failing to comply with the terms and conditions governing the distribution and sale of subsidised packet cooking oil.
The Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry also recorded eight cases of violations involving the sale and purchase of subsidised packet cooking oil by foreigners following the introduction of the Mobile eCOSS system and the enforcement of related regulations on March 1.
According to the ministry, the implementation of eCOSS since 2023 has enabled the monitoring of distribution chains and transactions, as well as digital verification of users' identities through electronic Know Your Customer (eKYC) and MyDigital ID.
A Cooking Oil Distribution Zoning Mechanism and a purchase limit of three packets per transaction have also been introduced to ensure adequate supplies and curb leakages.
"In this regard, to ensure that digitalisation does not hinder access, particularly for the elderly and those living in rural areas, the ministry will continue to refine and simplify transaction methods.
"One of the measures being implemented is the integration of eCOSS with the Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) programme and the National Registration Department, allowing the national identity card (MyKad) to be used for verification during purchases," the ministry said in a parliamentary written reply.
It said the effectiveness and suitability of the digital mechanism would be evaluated before any consideration was given to extending it to other subsidised goods, while balancing efforts to curb leakages with the need to ensure convenient access for consumers.
Meanwhile, the ministry recorded 5,893 cases involving the leakage and misappropriation of diesel, petrol and cooking oil nationwide between January 2023 and Oct 31, with seized items valued at RM82.85 million.
Of the total, 2,763 cases involved diesel, with seizures valued at RM59.67 million, followed by 1,722 petrol-related cases (RM5.43 million) and 1,408 cases involving packet cooking oil (RM17.74 million).
The ministry said enforcement efforts would continue to be strengthened through intelligence-led operations, data utilisation, rigorous monitoring and strategic cooperation with other agencies, including through Op Tiris 4.0 (Bersepadu), which has been in force since March 16.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: AI is increasing the speed of cyberattacks, insurance panel says
Article:
HARRISBURG: AI has increased the speed of cyberattacks if not tactics, while humans remain the weakest link at many organisations, according to a panel of insurance industry professionals.
NetDiligence convened the panel following the release of its annual Cyber Claims Study, which found that ransomware demands and payments have reached unprecedented levels.
Initial demands have reached as high as US$500 million, with confirmed payments as high as US$90 million.
Large companies were the hardest hit, accounting for over half of total incident costs but just three per cent of the data set.
New threats, including social engineering fraud, have emerged in recent years, forcing cyber insurers to adapt.
"Social engineering fraud and fund transfer fraud, it's a huge thing that's happening in every single industry, and particularly to SMEs, but really to everybody.
"And the challenge is it's actually very easy to underwrite, too, because there's not a lot we can underwrite to.
"All we can do is really look at any type of dual authentication or dual control that you're using when making a payment," Jeff Kulikowski, executive vice president of cyber/professional liability at Westfield Specialty, said.
Humans are often the way in for threat actors, Kulikowski said.
"It's always generated from somebody who may not be responsible for making a payment, gets a call from a vendor.
"They're super excited, they're angry, they're put under pressure, and they skip the dual authentication process to make sure that there's proper fraud protection done or fraud prevention done.
"So the industry typically sublimits this because the exposure has become so big and so difficult to contend with," Kulikowski said.
"Very rarely does an angry vendor make it through two or three levels of a corporation. I dare them to get to the accounts payable person because they know what they're doing. It's always when it goes out of network, and it's just a very difficult coverage to provide," Kulikowski added.
Karla Reffold, chief insights officer at Surefire Cyber, said that SMEs in particular could be more vigilant, since threat actors don't attack businesses by industry or size but, instead, by technological vulnerability.
"I can't believe I still hear it in 2026, organisations saying, 'We're too small to be a target. No one cares about us.' (That understanding) of how much your dollar is worth in other countries that are targeting us is just not there," Reffold said.
AI has also made threat actors more dangerous, primarily in terms of speed.
"The good news is that we are not seeing a huge shift in the tactics. We're not seeing a huge shift in how they gain access to organisations," Reffold said.
Juliet White, head of cyber at Howden US, said that insureds often have less coverage than they expect because they bought their policy years ago and inflation has driven costs up.
For SMEs, cyber insurance is also often less about the coverage than about the protection that comes with it, Westfield Specialty's  Kulikowski said.
"This product has become less of an insurance policy and more of a service platform, especially for SMEs, where they don't have the same IT platform, protection platform, scale as a US$30 billion company that has an almost unlimited budget to address these things," Kulikowski said.
Mark Greisiger, president of NetDiligence, which published the report, said that, even in larger organisations, leadership can be the ones most vulnerable.
"We increasingly hear they're targeting the most senior people in organisations, be it a law firm, be it an accounting firm, because those guys at the very top have a lot of credentials to move east and west throughout their network, and they can get things done," Greisiger said.
"And they do skip, I think, some of the baseline security processes."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Penang approves emergency slope works at Paya Terubong landslide site
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Emergency slope stabilisation works have been approved at the Taman Seri Rambai landslide site in Paya Terubong following the submission of a complete engineering proposal.
State Local Government, Town and Country Planning Committee chairman H'ng Mooi Lye said the Penang Department of Occupational Safety and Health (DOSH) received the complete documentation and formal application from Aptitude Consulting Engineers Sdn Bhd yesterday.
"Following the submission, DOSH has granted permission for the developer's civil engineer to carry out the mitigation works, subject to approvals and clearances from other relevant agencies," he said today.
The approved works are expected to take between four and five months. They include emergency surface drainage mitigation (ESCP) and slope stabilisation in the collapsed area, identified as Zone 1.
The works will also cover preventive stabilisation of exposed cut slopes at the construction site.
H'ng said the developer and contractor had been reminded to comply strictly with the Occupational Safety and Health Act 1994, as well as all regulations, requirements and directives issued by the relevant authorities.
Meanwhile, residents of the four evacuated houses are still not allowed to return home.
"They will only be allowed to return once the mitigation works in Zone 1 are fully completed and certified safe by a geotechnical engineer," he added.
The Oct 25 landslide at Taman Seri Rambai in Paya Terubong killed 73-year-old Dr Wong Kar Lin after debris struck his house. His wife and mother-in-law escaped unscathed.
State authorities have attributed responsibility for the tragedy to the developer and landowner of an adjacent condominium and road project.
Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said that they could face legal action, noting that the slope failure originated within their construction site.
At an inter-agency meeting chaired by H'ng on Nov 2 to assess the ongoing
investigations
and mitigation plans, the state said that any formal finding of liability or negligence would only be made after DOSH completes its investigation.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Najib's conditional pardon: Johor MB tells DAP, Amanah to seek Anwar's explanation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi said DAP and Amanah leaders, as well as the Bar Council, should seek clarification from Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim over Datuk Seri Najib Razak's conditional pardon and
house arrest
, instead of involving the palace.
Onn Hafiz said Anwar had brought forward and included the pardon application for Najib in the agenda of the Pardons Board meeting during a Dewan Rakyat sitting on Dec 10, 2024.
"This is their true nature, and this is not the first time former Damansara member of parliament Tony Pua and his DAP allies have incited controversy involving the royal institution.
"He (Tony Pua) was previously investigated by police following his remarks concerning the Sultan of Selangor's decree.
"Now, once again, the palace is being dragged into a political dispute. Disrespect and disloyalty towards the rulers must not be normalised," he said in a social media post.
He said every prisoner had the right to seek a pardon, while the power to grant pardons was the prerogative of the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, as provided for under Article 42 of the Federal Constitution.
"The decision is made by the Pardons Board, which includes representatives of the federal government and the Attorney-General," he said.
He said His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, had decreed that the conditional pardon was clear and must be respected.
"His Majesty also stressed that any arguments disputing the order were tantamount to defying the decree of the
Yang di-Pertuan Agong
.
"So why does Tony Pua still want the people to direct their questions to the palace? If there are questions about its implementation, ask the parties responsible. Do not make the palace a target of political disputes.
"Do not become so engrossed in politics that you forget the second principle of the Rukun Negara, Loyalty to the King and Country," he said.
Earlier, media reports said
Tony Pua
had allegedly mocked the King over the conditional pardon granted to Najib.

Title: Flood evacuees in Selangor, Perak rise to 1,444
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The number of flood evacuees in Selangor and Perak has risen to 1,444, with all of them seeking shelter at nine temporary relief centres as at 8.30am today.
The figure represents an increase of nine people from the 1,435 evacuees recorded at the same nine centres as at 10pm yesterday.
According to the Social Welfare Department's Info Bencana portal, Selangor recorded the highest number, with 1,138 evacuees from 315 families housed at seven relief centres in Kuala Selangor.
Perak recorded 302 evacuees from 91 families at two relief centres in Hilir Perak.
Of the total evacuees, 466 were adult women, 437 adult men, 219 girls, 283 boys, 27 baby boys and 12 baby girls.
