Title: Najib’s immediate family can stay with him during house arrest, Parliament told
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — Only immediate family members are permitted to reside in the same house as Datuk Seri Mohd Najib Razak under strict home detention conditions, which also prohibit the former prime minister from using personal mobile phones or appearing on social media, Parliament was told today.
Speaking during Minister’s Question Time this morning, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail outlined the specific terms stipulated by the Pardons Board governing Najib’s residence, movement, and communications.
Under the residential restrictions, Najib’s immediate family was specifically defined as his spouse, children, sons- and daughters-in-law, and grandchildren.
Anyone outside this immediate circle is barred from residing there without prior written approval.
“The Pardons Board specifies who is permitted to stay; only those individuals may reside there. Beyond that, prior written permission is required,” Saifuddin explained.
He added that Najib is strictly prohibited from moving to another house, building, or premise, and cannot leave the registered address, including to attend Friday prayers, without obtaining written authorisation.
Receiving guests at the residence is similarly prohibited unless prior written consent is granted and Saifuddin said Najib is barred from using any mobile phones or telecommunications devices, except equipment officially registered by the Prisons Department.
The former prime minister is also strictly prohibited from exposing himself to, or appearing in, any media coverage or on any social media platforms.
“The registered device is strictly for the Prisons Department to contact him and verify that he is at the residence,” he said.

Title: Govt studies proposal to extend EPF i-Sayang scheme to non-citizen wives
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — The government, through the Employees Provident Fund (EPF), will continue to study a proposal to expand the scope and coverage of the EPF i-Sayang scheme to allow Malaysian husbands to make voluntary contributions for their non-citizen wives.
The Finance Ministry (MOF) said the proposal would be studied carefully, taking into account the importance of protecting families’ retirement savings and ensuring the programme’s sustainability.
“The government takes note of the proposal to expand the eligibility criteria for i-Sayang recipients to allow non-citizen wives to receive transferred contributions from their Malaysian citizen husbands. The proposal requires careful consideration to ensure that any expansion remains aligned with the original objectives of i-Sayang and the EPF’s retirement savings policy framework.
“In this regard, the suitability of its implementation must be carefully assessed, including its implications for retirement savings protection and objectives, as well as legal, governance, operational and programme sustainability aspects, before further consideration is given,” the ministry said in a written parliamentary reply published on Parliament’s website yesterday.
The MOF was responding to a question from Rodziah Ismail (PH-Ampang) on the strategies and implementation mechanisms for the proposed expansion of the EPF i-Sayang scheme to allow Malaysian husbands to make voluntary contributions for their non-citizen wives, given that non-citizen husbands are already allowed to do so for their Malaysian citizen wives.
i-Sayang is a government initiative that allows husbands to voluntarily transfer two per cent of their employee contributions to their wives’ EPF accounts.
Since its introduction in March 2023, a total of 233,371 husbands nationwide have registered as contributors, involving 233,547 wives as recipients.
As at August 31, 2026, a total of RM563.6 million had been transferred through i-Sayang. — Bernama

Title: Penang exco defends RM8.4b Perak water deal, says charge covers dedicated plant over 40 years
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Nov 12 — The Penang state government has defended the RM8.4 billion capacity charge under its conditional water supply agreement with Perak, saying the payment covers a treatment plant dedicated to the state and is spread over 40 years.
State Infrastructure, Transport and Digital Committee chairman Zairil Khir Johari said the charge was a deferred payment for the construction and financing of the plant, which would be built solely to supply treated water to Penang.
"The plant costs RM3 billion to construct. If we include 40-year financing and refurbishment costs, it sums up to RM8.4 billion, a figure that has withstood the scrutiny of financial consultants appointed to conduct due diligence on the project," he said in a statement today.
He said the conditional Bulk Water Supply Agreement (BWSA) between Perbadanan Bekalan Air Pulau Pinang Sdn Bhd (PBAPP) and Prasarana Air dan Irigasi Perak Sdn Bhd (PAIP) was a government-to-government agreement aimed at ensuring Penang's future water security.
Under the agreement, Penang would receive between 300 and 500 million litres a day (MLD) of treated water for the next 40 years and beyond.
Zairil said Perak would be fully responsible for the construction and financing risks of the 500 MLD treatment plant, which would be dedicated solely to supplying PBAPP, as well as its maintenance and upgrading throughout the agreement.
"PBAPP makes no upfront payment or capital contribution to PAIP, and repays the plant cost through the annual capacity charge from the supply start date, stretched over 40 years to make it more affordable to PBAPP," he said.
He said the annual capacity charge of RM210 million would reserve the plant's capacity for Penang while covering its construction and financing costs.
Zairil also clarified that the capacity charge was separate from the supply charge, which would only apply to water actually delivered.
"The supply charge is the price of the water, and is not charged on water that PAIP fails to deliver," he said.
He added that building a desalination plant would cost more than the BWSA arrangement.
"PBAPP’s internal estimates put the capital and lifecycle cost of a typical 300 MLD desalination plant above RM25 billion, for a plant with a typical lifespan of about 20 years while in comparison, the capacity charge sums up to a total of RM8.4 billion over 40 years," he said.
Zairil said the PBA Holdings Bhd (PBAHB) board, including five dissenting directors, agreed that the water purchase was necessary for Penang's long-term water security.
He said the state's water demand was projected to exceed 1,100 MLD by 2032, while it remained reliant on Sungai Muda.
"The dissenting directors’ reservations are confined to the issue of payment terms in the event of Perak’s ‘state interest clause’ kicking in and prolonged suspension," he said.
Addressing these concerns, Zairil said Penang was protected under the agreement, as RM16.2 billion of the RM24.6 billion in total projected payments comprised supply charges for the water itself.
"In the event of a quantity or quality shortfall, PBAPP pays supply charges only on actual water delivered that meets the pre-agreed quality," he said.
He added that PAIP would have to pay PBAPP liquidated damages for water supply shortfalls, at the same rate PBAPP paid for water delivered.
However, the damages would not apply to shortfalls caused by circumstances beyond PAIP's control, such as severe drought, or when Perak's own water needs took priority under the state interest clause.
"Priority for the host’s needs is common practice where a state or country’s resources are involved, and akin to the national interest clause in petroleum production sharing contracts (PSCs) which allows the federal government to override contractual operations to prioritise domestic needs," he said.
Zairil said Penang could also terminate the agreement and claim damages if PAIP breached its terms and failed to remedy the breach within 90 days, or if PAIP became insolvent.
In the event of a supply suspension lasting more than three months through no fault of PBAPP, either party could request renegotiation and seek mediation by the respective state governments.
If renegotiation failed after another three months, either party could terminate the agreement.
In such circumstances, PBAPP would have to make a single payment equivalent to the remaining capacity charges, discounted at four per cent per annum, with the amount decreasing each year the plant operated.
However, if PAIP's licence was not renewed through no fault of either party, the agreement would end without PBAPP having to pay any further capacity charges.
Zairil said PBAPP could also exit the agreement in the 22nd contract year if both parties failed to agree on a review of the supply charge, subject to payment of the remaining capacity charges discounted at four per cent per annum.
He said the agreement should be considered in its entirety, as individual clauses could appear one-sided when viewed in isolation.
“Read as a whole, its terms allocate risk between both parties fairly,” he said.

Title: Four suspects rob man of RM10,000 after approaching him for donations at Permatang Pauh petrol station
Article:
BUKIT MERTAJAM, Nov 12 — A 43-year-old man was injured after being robbed by four individuals believed to be foreigners using sharp metal objects at the entrance to a petrol station along Jalan Samagagah, Permatang Pauh, here yesterday.
Seberang Perai Tengah district police chief ACP Nik Aminuddin Raja Abdullah said the incident, which occurred at about 11.30am, was believed to have involved two men and two women suspected to be foreigners from Central Asian countries.
“In the incident, the suspects are believed to have acted aggressively and used sharp metal objects, causing injuries to the victim before fleeing with his personal belongings, with total losses estimated at RM10,000.
“The group's modus operandi was to solicit monetary donations from members of the public at the petrol station before committing robbery,” he said in a statement last night.
He urged members of the public with information on the incident to contact investigating officer ASP Marsila Hamzah at 019-472 5217 to assist in the investigation.
He also advised the public to remain vigilant and not be easily deceived by such tactics, and to seek assistance and protection at petrol stations immediately if they encounter suspicious situations or threats. — Bernama

Title: Malaysian Bar mounts fresh challenge against Najib’s house arrest
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — The Malaysian Bar has filed a fresh legal action challenging the Federal Territories Pardons Board's decision allowing former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak to serve the remainder of his prison sentence in the SRC International Sdn Bhd case under house arrest.
The Bar filed the application for leave of judicial review on November 10 at the High Court here, naming the Federal Territories Pardons Board, Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform), Director-General of Prisons and Najib as respondents.
The media obtained the documents yesterday. The application will be heard before Justice S. Indra Nehru today.
In the application, the Bar seeks a declaration that any proceedings or decision purportedly made under Articles 40 and 42 of the Federal Constitution is invalid in law and contradicts the Federal Constitution.
This includes the decision announced through a media statement dated September 18, 2026 by the second respondent, allowing Najib to serve the remainder of his sentence by way of “house arrest” or “home detention.”
The Bar further seeks an order to quash the Pardons Board's proceedings and decision, as well as an order for the house arrest of the former prime minister to be stayed immediately, should leave be granted, pending the outcome of the judicial review. — Bernama

Title: ‘When in doubt, shoot’: KL police chief orders men not to hesitate following machete attack on constable
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — City police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus has directed officers never to hesitate in drawing and discharging their service firearms against violent resistance, following a vicious machete attack on Wednesday that severed a policeman's hand.
Fadil stressed that frontline personnel must take immediate defensive action to protect their lives rather than risk suffering the same catastrophic harm.
"So, as I have said, you must always be ready. You must know how to draw your weapons: Ready, draw, fire.
"If there is any resistance, shoot. When in doubt, shoot. If there is concern or threat, shoot. Do not wait," Fadil said in an operational address shared online.
His reminder came after a bloody altercation at a residential flat in Desa Aman Puri, Kepong. Selangor Police Chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said that authorities mobilised around 4pm after the public reported an aggressive foreign man exhibiting unstable behaviour.
A multi-agency team comprising police, Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) responders, and Health Ministry personnel arrived at the scene to de-escalate the situation. The moment the unit breached the apartment door, the suspect lunged forward wielding two machetes.
A 26-year-old lance corporal attached to the Gombak District Police Headquarters Mobile Patrol Vehicle (MPV) unit bore the brunt of the onslaught, having his right wrist severed alongside deep lacerations across his head and torso. Several firefighters and medical personnel sustained minor injuries during the clash.
The assailant slipped away from the building but was cornered roughly four hours later at a neighbouring playground. When the suspect attempted a second machete assault against arresting officers, police opened fire. He succumbed to gunshot wounds while being transported to the hospital.
First responders rushed the injured lance corporal to Selayang Hospital before transferring him to Hospital Kuala Lumpur, where a specialist surgical team operated on his severed hand.
He remains in stable condition as footage and images of the bloody incident continue to circulate widely across Malaysian social media.

Title: Court of Appeal clears Felda Palm Industries of effluent discharge offence, orders RM18,000 refund
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Nov 12 — The Court of Appeal yesterday set aside Felda Palm Industries Sdn Bhd's conviction and RM18,000 fine for discharging effluent with content exceeding the prescribed limits.
A three-member panel comprising Justices Datuk Azman Abdullah, Datuk Noorin Badaruddin and Datuk Meor Hashimi Abdul Hamid allowed the company’s appeal to set aside the Sessions Court decision that convicted it of the offence and imposed the fine.
Delivering a unanimous decision, Justice Azman said doubts over the handling and preservation of the effluent samples by the Department of Environment undermined the accuracy of the Chemistry Department of Malaysia's analysis.
He added that the company had submitted analysis results showing a lower three-day Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD) reading, and that the prosecution had not adduced any rebuttal evidence.
Justice Azman ordered that the RM18,000 fine paid by the company be refunded.
On September 17, 2021, the Kuantan Sessions Court acquitted and discharged Felda Palm Industries without calling for its defence at the close of the prosecution's case on the charge.
However, on January 14, 2022, the High Court allowed the prosecutor's appeal and ordered the case to be remitted to the Sessions Court to hear the company's defence.
On August 8, 2023, the Sessions Court convicted Felda Palm Industries and imposed an RM18,000 fine, with 30 days' imprisonment in default of payment, while the High Court dismissed the company's appeal and upheld the Sessions Court's decision on January 16 this year.
According to the charge, Felda Palm Industries was accused of discharging effluent with a three-day BOD content of 130 mg/l at 30 degrees Celsius.
The reading exceeded the prescribed limit of 100 mg/l set under Condition No. 5 of the Second Schedule, Regulation 12(3) of the Environmental Quality (Prescribed Premises) (Crude Palm Oil) Regulations 1977, and Licence Compliance Schedule No. 003243 issued under Section 18(1) of the Environmental Quality Act 1974.
The company was accused of committing the offence at its premises at Kilang Sawit Selancar 2A, Rancangan Felda Selancar 2, Rompin District, Pahang, at 10.45am on July 24, 2018.
Felda Palm Industries was charged with the offence under Section 16(1) of the Environmental Quality Act 1974.
Selancar 2A palm oil mill manager Muhammad Azam Raja Ibrahim attended the proceedings yesterday on behalf of the company.
Deputy public prosecutor Mohamed Aznin Mohamed Ariff appeared for the prosecution, while lawyers Datuk Habizan Rahman Habeeb Rahman, Sarina Alwi and Hanif Asyraf Mohd Salleh represented Felda Palm Industries. — Bernama

Title: ‘A man of principle’: Ramanan says Anthony Loke’s resignation a major loss for govt
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan has described Anthony Loke Siew Fook’s decision to resign as Transport Minister as a major loss to the government.
“I am sad. He is a good friend and was my Cabinet colleague. I will miss him, but this is his decision and position. He is a man of principle and we have to accept it. This is a major loss,” he said here yesterday.
He was speaking to reporters after attending the Socso ‘I Lindung U’ 2026 Media Awards here.
Yesterday, Loke announced his immediate resignation as Transport Minister following the Kuala Lumpur High Court’s decision to allow former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest.
In another development, Ramanan said any Cabinet reshuffle was within the Prime Minister’s purview and that he had not received any notification about one so far.
Yesterday, Anwar said it was not yet time to consider a Cabinet reshuffle, following the impending end of Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan’s term as a Dewan Negara member on December 11.
Commenting on Saturday’s Melaka state election, Ramanan, who is also a vice-president of Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR), urged voters to turn out and elect their new representatives.
“I hope all the people of Melaka will fulfil their responsibility and come out in large numbers to vote. This is important because it is your right and your decision on who will lead the state,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Pan Borneo Highway delays not always contractors’ fault, says Nanta
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — Contracts of companies involved in the construction of the Pan Borneo Highway cannot be terminated arbitrarily, as delays in individual work packages are not necessarily caused solely by the contractors’ shortcomings.
Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi said that when contractors applied for an extension of time (EOT), the Works Ministry (KKR) had to assess whether the delays were caused by constraints on the part of government agencies or other factors.
He said only one contractor had so far had its contract terminated over delays in the project, following a comprehensive assessment.
“When contractors apply for an extension of time, we have to carefully examine whether the problem is their fault, as some delays may also be caused by factors on our side.
“For example, a contractor may be ready to begin work but cannot access the site because land acquisition and compensation matters have yet to be settled by the relevant government department,” he said.
Nanta said this after appearing as a guest on a recording of Bernama TV’s Ruang Bicara programme that discussed strengthening national infrastructure towards sustainable development, scheduled to be aired on November 16.
Apart from land compensation issues, Nanta said construction work could also be held up if utility infrastructure, such as water pipes and underground cables, had yet to be relocated by the relevant parties, as proceeding with the work could risk damaging them.
To avoid further delays, he said KKR had proactively set up monitoring committees, a steering committee and task forces to address the issues.
“Through these platforms, problems at construction sites can be raised and solutions decided immediately, without having to wait unnecessarily and waste time due to poor coordination,” he said.
Nanta said oversight of the projects was also being strengthened through regular site visits by the ministry's top management, as well as close cooperation with the Sabah and Sarawak Public Works Departments.
To date, only 11.4 per cent of the work packages under the Pan Borneo Highway project in Sabah have been completed, more than 10 years after its implementation began, while the Sarawak stretch is nearing completion. — Bernama

Title: Paya Terubong landslide: Four evacuated homes to remain off-limits for up to five months
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Nov 12 — Residents of four evacuated houses in Taman Seri Rambai, Paya Terubong, will not be allowed to return home until mitigation works at the landslide site are completed, state executive councillor H’ng Mooi Lye said today.
The local government and town and country planning committee chairman said the works were expected to take four to five months.
"As for the four evacuated houses, residents are still not permitted to return to their homes until the mitigation works in Zone 1 have been fully completed and verified by the geotechnical engineer," he said in a statement today.
He said the Penang Department of Occupational Safety and Health (DOSH) received full documentation and a formal application from Aptitude Consulting Engineers Sdn Bhd yesterday to carry out emergency mitigation and slope stabilisation works at the construction site affected by the landslide.
"DOSH granted permission to the developer’s civil engineer to carry out the mitigation works, subject to approval and permission from other relevant agencies," he said.
"The mitigation works permitted by DOSH include emergency surface drainage mitigation works (ESCP) and slope stabilisation in the landslide area (Zone 1), as well as preventive stabilisation works on the exposed cut slopes at the construction site," he said.
He reminded the developer and contractor to comply fully with the Occupational Safety and Health Act 1994 and all regulations and instructions issued by relevant agencies.
The Penang Island City Council (MBPP) had previously declared four houses, numbered 1, 3, 5 and 7, unsafe for occupation, while two others, numbered 9 and 11, were cleared for reoccupation.
The October 25 landslide killed 73-year-old doctor Wong Kar Lin, who was buried by earth that also affected his home.
His wife, Chang Mei Nuo, 68, and mother-in-law, Wong Poh Lim, who is in her 80s, managed to escape.

Title: Ramanan: HR Ministry to table new commuter protection, post-maternity allowance in December
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — Amendments to the Self-Employment Social Security Act 2017 (Act 789) and the Employment Insurance System Act 2017 (Act 800) will be tabled in Parliament in December.
Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said the proposed amendments to Act 789 would involve the Commuter Scheme, while those to Act 800 would cover the Post-Maternity Leave Allowance (EPCB).
He said the amendments to Act 789 were aimed at strengthening social protection for Malaysians who commute across borders for work, particularly the more than 400,000 Malaysians who travel to Singapore daily.
“Towards the end of December, I will personally table the amendments to Act 789 relating to the Commuter Scheme, which will benefit Malaysians who commute to work abroad,” he said here yesterday.
He was speaking at the Social Security Organisation (PERKESO) i-LINDUNG Media Awards 2026 and Deepavali Celebration with the Media.
Also present were Deputy Human Resources Minister Datuk Khairul Firdaus Akbar Khan, PERKESO Board chairman Datuk Seri Subahan Kamal, PERKESO chief executive Datuk Seri Dr Mohammed Azman Aziz Mohammed, and Malaysian National News Agency (Bernama) Editor-in-Chief Arul Rajoo Durar Raj.
Ramanan said the amendments to Act 800 would involve the introduction of the EPCB, which is expected to benefit more than 132,000 women workers.
Both amendments were part of the government's efforts, through the Human Resources Ministry (KESUMA), to strengthen social protection and safeguard the people's welfare, he added.
He also called on the media to help disseminate information about the two initiatives so that more people would be aware of, understand and benefit from the facilities provided. — Bernama

Title: Anwar says RM7.5b Budget allocation will help Bumiputera contractors expand
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — The increase in Budget 2027 funding for Bumiputera G1 to G4 contractors to RM7.5 billion aims to help small contractors build their capabilities, expand their businesses and undertake projects needed by the people, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said in a Facebook post yesterday that the allocation had been discussed during an engagement session with representatives of Bumiputera contractors’ associations, which focused on ensuring the budget initiatives benefited small contractors.
“I want these opportunities to help produce more competitive and ethical Bumiputera contractors. Every project is a trust placed in us by the people and must be carried out to the highest standard, on schedule and with full responsibility,” he said.
The allocation has been raised to RM7.5 billion from RM4 billion this year and Anwar said procurement procedures had also been simplified, including raising the direct appointment limit for government facility maintenance and repair works to RM200,000.
The measures also included financing facilities and steps to address rising diesel and bitumen costs, he added. — Bernama

Title: Zahid says Negeri Sembilan political crisis in final stage, solution expected soon
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 12 — Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi is confident that the political crisis in Negeri Sembilan will be resolved soon.
The Deputy Prime Minister said he hoped a solution could be reached through a spirit of togetherness among the parties concerned, which had also enabled the formation of the state government previously.
“I am confident that whatever problems we are facing in Negeri Sembilan have reached their final stage. We pray that the issues will be resolved in the near future, Insya-Allah,” he said.
Ahmad Zahid, who is also Umno president, was speaking at the Perikatan Nasional (PN)-BN Grand Finale Ceramah programme here last night.
Also present were PAS deputy president Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man and Kelantan Menteri Besar Datuk Mohd Nassuruddin Daud. — Bernama

Title: Cabinet reshuffle no reason to dissolve Parliament, says Fuziah
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — The dissolution of Parliament should not be proposed simply because of questions surrounding a Cabinet reshuffle when the government remains functional and commands majority support, said Deputy Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Fuziah Salleh.
She said that after nearly four years of the Unity Government, the country should be able to focus on more pressing priorities, including investment, job opportunities, the cost of living and the long-standing institutional reform agenda.
“That is why I believe the proposal to dissolve Parliament when the government is still functioning and has majority support should not be raised lightly, especially when the original issue concerns only a Cabinet reshuffle.
“A Cabinet reshuffle is part of the process of strengthening the administration. It should not be used as a reason to reopen an episode of political uncertainty that we have experienced before,” she said in a Facebook post yesterday.
The Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) secretary-general said the political instability between 2020 and 2022, when the country was grappling with the COVID-19 pandemic, job losses and cost-of-living pressures, should serve as a lesson on the importance of maintaining a stable government.
She said efforts to strengthen governance, combat corruption and improve national institutions required policy continuity and a stable administration to ensure that the benefits reached the people.
Differences of opinion among leaders, she added, could be discussed without undermining the stability the country was working to build.
Fuziah also cautioned against allowing political interests to take precedence over the nation's future and the well-being of the people, who had long borne the consequences of political uncertainty.
Recently, certain quarters have called for Parliament to be dissolved instead of proceeding with a Cabinet reshuffle, following the approaching end of the term of Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan as a Dewan Negara member on December 11. — Bernama

Title: Guan Eng says two-year push for non-Bumi funding has failed to sway Anwar, but will keep pressing
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — DAP adviser Lim Guan Eng today said his repeated appeals to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim over the past two years for additional government allocations for non-Bumiputera communities have been unsuccessful.
The Bagan MP said he had personally raised the proposal with Anwar during meetings and in Parliament, amid criticism from political activists over his failure to secure the allocations.
“I admit that I have made these suggestion for the past 2 years to the Prime Minister personally in meetings with him and in my speeches in Parliament without success.”
“However, this failure would not deter me from continuing to speak out not just on this issue but also fight for economic and social justice for all communities and every Malaysian,” he said in a statement today.
He proposed that annual allocations for non-Bumiputeras be equivalent to 10 per cent of those specifically allocated to Bumiputeras, without reducing existing Bumiputera allocations.
Despite the setback, Lim said Anwar had adopted ten other economic proposals following repeated appeals from him and senior DAP leaders.
These included raising the e-invoicing exemption threshold to RM3 million in annual turnover, increasing individual income tax relief to RM12,000 from 2027 and restoring the Budi95 fuel subsidy quota to 300 litres per month.
“This shows that the Prime Minister is willing to listen and can be persuaded,” he said.
However, Lim said further reforms were needed to support 1.2 million micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) facing difficulties obtaining loans, rising compliance costs and competition from foreign businesses.
“Together with top DAP leaders, I will bring these people-centric issues up again in Parliament and in meetings with the Prime Minister,” he said.

Title: Anwar calls for firm action after policeman’s wrist severed in Kepong attack
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has condemned the attack on a policeman whose right wrist was severed by a foreign national in Kepong yesterday afternoon.
Anwar said all forms of crime and violence, particularly against enforcement personnel tasked with protecting public safety, were entirely unacceptable.
“Firm action must be taken against any criminal act, regardless of who commits it, to uphold the rule of law and ensure the safety of enforcement personnel on duty.
“I pray that the officer makes a speedy recovery,” he said in a Facebook post yesterday.
Selangor Police Chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said yesterday that the police personnel was being treated at Kuala Lumpur Hospital and was in stable condition. — Bernama

Title: Suspect shot dead after severing policeman’s wrist with machete in Kepong (VIDEO)
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — A policeman’s right wrist was severed after he was attacked by a foreign national who went on a rampage at a residential property in Desa Aman Puri, Kepong, this afternoon.
Selangor Police Chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said police received a report from a member of the public at 4pm about a man who was reportedly in an unstable condition and behaving aggressively.
Following the report, a team of police, Malaysian Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) personnel and Health Ministry (MOH) staff was sent to the scene to help control the situation.
When the door was opened, the suspect attacked the officers with two machetes and caused a 26-year-old Lance Corporal from the Gombak District Police Headquarters’ Mobile Patrol Vehicle (MPV) unit to suffer a severed right wrist and injuries to his head and body.
“Several firefighters and MOH personnel also sustained minor injuries. The suspect then fled but was located at a nearby playground at 8pm,” he told a press conference at Selayang Hospital here last night.
Shazeli said the suspect attacked police with a machete when officers tried to arrest him, prompting them to fire several shots.
He said the suspect was pronounced dead while being taken to hospital.
The injured policeman was taken to Selayang Hospital before being transferred to Kuala Lumpur Hospital for surgery on his severed right hand and he was reported to be in stable condition.
The incident had earlier gone viral on social media, drawing various reactions from netizens. — Bernama

Title: Still paying for an unfinished home in Malaysia? Here’s what Budget 2027 offers affected buyers
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 12 — Thousands of Malaysians who bought homes in abandoned housing projects are still waiting for answers, uncertain whether their properties will ever be completed or what they can do next.
For some, the financial burden continues, with housing loans to repay despite having no home to move into.
Budget 2027 proposes measures to ease some of these costs and encourage developers to revive abandoned housing projects.
But the assistance comes with conditions, and the government is not offering to settle buyers’ outstanding housing loans.
So what help is available, and what steps can affected purchasers take?
Here’s what you need to know.
What qualifies as an abandoned housing project?
A housing project may be classified as abandoned under several circumstances, including when construction has stopped for six consecutive months, the developer has been placed under receivership, a winding-up petition has been filed, or the developer admits it cannot continue with the development.
A project must also be formally declared abandoned by the minister under the Housing Development (Control and Licensing) Act 1966.
As of August 31, 2026, the Housing and Local Government Ministry (KPKT) had identified 262 abandoned private housing projects in Peninsular Malaysia.
Of these, 99 were licensed projects involving 28,289 housing units, while another 163 were unlicensed projects involving 10,605 units.
What assistance does Budget 2027 offer?
The government has proposed reinstating a full stamp duty exemption for transactions involving the rehabilitation of abandoned housing developments.
According to the Finance Ministry’s Budget 2027 Tax Measures, the exemption covers two groups: rescue contractors or developers brought in to rehabilitate abandoned housing projects, and original purchasers of properties in those developments.
The proposed exemption applies to eligible loan agreements and instruments of transfer executed between January 1, 2027, and December 31, 2030, subject to certification by KPKT.
For original purchasers, this means loan agreements for additional financing and property transfers connected to the rehabilitation process may qualify for full stamp duty relief.
For rescue developers and contractors, the exemption is intended to reduce transaction costs associated with taking over and financing abandoned developments.
The government previously offered a similar exemption for eligible transactions executed between January 1, 2013, and December 31, 2025.
Its proposed reinstatement is intended to encourage more rehabilitation efforts by reducing some of the costs involved in rescuing unfinished developments.
Will the government pay buyers’ outstanding loans?
No. The stamp duty exemption does not mean the government will settle the outstanding housing loans of affected purchasers.
Under KPKT’s existing guidance, buyers may still have to meet their housing loan repayment obligations under their financing agreements, even when their housing projects have been abandoned.
However, buyers whose projects have been officially declared abandoned can obtain a confirmation letter from KPKT to support applications for financial assistance.
According to the National Housing Department, the letter can help purchasers seek consideration for:
Lower housing loan interest rates
Restructuring of loan repayments
A second Employees Provident Fund (EPF) withdrawal to purchase another home
For government employees with financing from the Public Sector Home Financing Board (LPPSA), the letter can also support applications to:
Cancel an existing housing loan and apply for a new one
Defer the 4 per cent interest charge during the project’s rehabilitation period or for five years, whichever comes first
These arrangements are subject to applications and approval by the respective institutions. They are not automatic entitlements.
How can buyers get official confirmation?
Buyers can check whether their housing development is officially listed as abandoned through KPKT’s housing information portal, Transforming and Empowering Data Usage in Housing (TEDUH).
If the project is listed, purchasers can apply for a confirmation letter from the National Housing Department.
The letter provides official confirmation of the project’s status and allows purchasers to approach their banks, EPF or LPPSA to seek the relevant assistance.
Applications can be submitted by email to pa_ppt@kpkt.gov.my, together with copies of the applicant’s identity card and sale and purchase agreement.
If the development is not listed, purchasers can seek clarification from the National Housing Department’s Private Housing Project Monitoring Division.
Buyers can also check the rehabilitation status of their developments through KPKT’s portal.
What if the developer cannot complete the project?
When a housing project is abandoned, buyers may face difficulties recovering the money they have already paid, particularly if the developer is insolvent or undergoing liquidation.
KPKT advises purchasers to submit claims against the developer by registered post or complete a Proof of Debt form obtainable from the Insolvency Department of Malaysia.
The ministry also stresses the importance of acting within the applicable limitation period.
Under the Limitation Act 1953, contractual claims are generally subject to a six-year limitation period, although when that period begins depends on when the cause of action arises.
KPKT’s published guidance refers to a six-year period from the date the sale and purchase agreement was signed.
Given the potential legal consequences of missing a deadline, affected purchasers should seek legal advice on the limitation period applicable to their claims.
How many projects have been revived?
According to figures released on October 19, KPKT said 1,726 troubled private housing projects involving 199,643 residential units, with a combined gross development value of RM158.16 billion, had been rehabilitated between 2023 and August 2026.
The figure covers both sick and abandoned developments.
Of the 1,726 troubled projects addressed between 2023 and August 2026:
1,542 sick projects involving 163,621 housing units were completed and obtained their Certificates of Completion and Compliance (CCC)
147 sick projects involving 29,900 units were restored to satisfactory progress
37 abandoned projects involving 6,122 units were rehabilitated through physical completion or other arrangements benefiting homebuyers
KPKT defines a sick housing project as one where construction progress is more than 30 per cent behind schedule, or where the completion period stipulated in the sale and purchase agreement (SPA) has expired.
However, a sick project is not automatically classified as abandoned.
Can Malaysia end abandoned housing projects by 2030?
The government has set a target of eliminating sick and abandoned private housing projects by 2030.
To achieve this, KPKT established the Task Force for Sick and Abandoned Private Housing Projects (TFST) in 2023 to coordinate rehabilitation efforts involving developers, financial institutions, purchasers and other relevant parties.
The task force monitors troubled developments and facilitates recovery measures.
The ministry is also strengthening oversight through measures including the Housing Integrated Management System (HIMS), TEDUH and periodic audits of Housing Development Accounts.
These initiatives are intended to identify troubled developments earlier and prevent more buyers from being left with unfinished homes.

Title: Flood season brings lucrative catfish haul for Kinta river fishermen in Perak
Article:
TELUK INTAN, Nov 12 — Whenever the water level of the Kinta River rises during the rainy season, Anuar Osman knows it is time to head to the river and set up
belat
(traditional fish traps) in anticipation of the arrival of
ikan lundu
(a type of catfish), which provides him with a supplementary source of income.
For the 49-year-old inland fisherman, catching
ikan lundu
is not his main occupation but rather a seasonal opportunity that he seizes whenever the fish migrate in schools through the river.
With catches sometimes exceeding 100 kilogrammes a day, the
ikan lundu
not only fill his traps but also bring in extra income when sold to wholesalers.
Anuar, who also manages an oil palm smallholding, said the large-scale appearance of
ikan lundu
typically lasts for about a week, depending on the river’s water level.
He explained that as the water rises, the fish move into areas where the
belat
are positioned along the river’s course. However, fishing activities come to a halt once the water level recedes.
Whenever the water level of the Kinta River rises during the rainy season, inland fishermen in Teluk Intan know it is time to head to the river and set up traditional fish traps, known as ‘belat’, in anticipation of the arrival of ‘lundu’ catfish (Arius maculatus), which provide an additional source of income. — Bernama pic
“When we see the water rising, the fish will appear for about a week, but once the river level drops, we stop fishing,” he told Bernama when met in Kampung Permatang Pelanduk, near here, today.
He added that using
belat
is more effective than nets for catching
ikan lundu
, as the fish have sharp spines that make them difficult to remove from nets.
Another inland fisherman, 37-year-old Shahril Yeop Mat Sibi, who works as a school canteen assistant, also takes advantage of the opportunity to catch
ikan lundu
whenever the water rises in the Kinta River.
Based on his observations, the fish migrate from the lower reaches of the Perak River into the Kinta River, eventually entering the
belat
set up at strategic locations along the riverbanks.
He said the traps do not require bait, as the
ikan lundu
move in schools and enter them by following the river’s current.
Inland fisherman Anuar Osman, 49, speaks to a Bernama reporter at Kampung Pematang Pelanduk, November 10, 2026. — Bernama pic
“As long as the
belat
is not full, the fish will continue entering. Once it is full, we quickly pull it up because more fish from downstream will keep moving upstream.
“That is the bounty brought by the floods. The fish travel in schools, and for about a week, as long as the river remains deep,
lundu
(catfish) appear in large numbers,” he said.
Shahril said the catch could reach up to 100 kilogrammes a day, providing a worthwhile supplementary income despite the short fishing season.
Meanwhile, fish trader Mohd Jasnurol Iznal Zainal Abidin, 43, said
lundu
is among the main species sold at his freshwater fish collection and distribution centre, operated under the Fisheries Development Authority of Malaysia (LKIM) in Parit 9, Kampung Gajah, during the flood season.
Inland fisherman Shahril Yeop Mat Sibi, 37, checks a traditional fish trap, known as a ‘belat’, set up at a strategic location along the banks of the Kinta River in Kampung Pematang Pelanduk. — Bernama pic
The father of five said he could sell between 300 and 600 kilogrammes of
lundu
daily at about RM30 per kilogramme, depending on supplies from local fishermen.
“I source the
lundu
from local fishermen, who consider the flood season the best time to catch this species. The highest volume I have ever sold was about two tonnes in a single day last year,” said Mohd Jasnurol, who also supplies the fish to the Selayang Wholesale Market.
However, despite the prospect of additional earnings, the fishing activity is not without risks, particularly the presence of crocodiles in the river, which poses a threat to fishermen who may encounter the reptiles while checking their traps.
He advised those involved in similar activities to remain vigilant and never underestimate river conditions, especially when water levels rise and currents become stronger. — Bernama

Title: Anwar, Wan Azizah convey condolences over Melaka PKR leader J. Samivel’s passing
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and his wife Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail have extended their condolences to the family of Alor Gajah PKR branch vice-chief J. Samivel, who died in a road accident in Jasin earlier today.
Anwar, who is also Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman, said in a Facebook post today that Samivel, 62, was also the representative for P. Denesh, the PH candidate for the Asahan seat in the Melaka state election.
“Samivel had served the party for many years and remained steadfast in its struggle. May his contributions and spirit continue to guide us as we carry on this struggle.
“My thoughts and prayers, together with Azizah, are with his family and comrades. May they be given strength and fortitude in facing this difficult trial,” he said.
Jasin police chief Supt Lee Robert said police received a report about the accident involving the car Samivel was travelling in at Jalan Pondok Batang, Jasin, at about 12.45 pm today. — Bernama

Title: Cabinet to be briefed on latest constitutional amendments separating AG, Public Prosecutor roles
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11— The Parliamentary Special Select Committee (JKPK) on Constitutional Amendments Relating to the Separation of the Roles of the Attorney-General and Public Prosecutor has decided that the latest proposed amendments to the Federal Constitution on the reform be brought to the Cabinet’s attention.
In a statement today, the committee said the decision was made after hearing a presentation and feedback from the Attorney-General’s Chambers (AGC) on the proposed amendments, following its review of matters raised at the 270th Meeting of the Conference of Rulers.
“The committee examined the proposed amendments submitted by the AGC, particularly to ensure that the matters raised by the Conference of Rulers receive due consideration in strengthening the legal framework for implementing the reform, in line with the principles of constitutional monarchy and the supremacy of the Federal Constitution,” the statement said.
The committee also reaffirmed its commitment to ensuring that the separation of the roles of the Attorney-General and Public Prosecutor is implemented carefully and in accordance with the Constitution to strengthen the independence of the prosecution institution, accountability and public confidence in the country’s justice system.
The meeting was chaired by Pengerang Member of Parliament, who is also Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform), Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said.
Also present were Parit Sulong MP and Plantation and Commodities Minister Datuk Seri Dr Noraini Ahmad, William Leong Jee Keen (Selayang), Syahredzan Johan (Bangi), Ramkarpal Singh (Bukit Gelugor), Datuk Seri Dr Ronald Kiandee (Beluran), Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan (Kota Bharu) and Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman (Muar).
Larut MP and Opposition Leader Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin, Alor Gajah MP and Deputy Defence Minister Adly Zahari, Datuk Lo Su Fui (Tawau) and Roy Angau Gingkoi (Lubok Antu) were unable to attend the meeting due to unavoidable circumstances. — Bernama

Title: Nine-year-old boy killed in suspected crocodile attack in Kudat
Article:
KUDAT, Nov 11 — A nine-year-old boy was killed in a suspected crocodile attack while trying to retrieve a fishing hook caught in Sungai Semayan, Kampung Semayan, Pulau Banggi, today.
The victim, identified as Mohamad Hilmi Nurjahid, was a Year Three pupil of Sekolah Kebangsaan Semayan.
Kudat District Police Chief Supt Mohd Haris Ibrahim said the incident occurred at about 3.30pm while the boy was fishing with his elder brother.
He said the boy went into the river to free his fishing hook but subsequently disappeared, believed to have been snatched by a crocodile.
A search and rescue operation involving police, Civil Defence Force personnel and villagers was launched after a report was received at about 4.30pm.
The boy was found by his father at about 8.10pm beneath Sungai Semayan Bridge, not far from where he was last seen.

Title: Anwar hails Malaysia’s leap to 27th globally in digital, AI competitiveness
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — Malaysia has climbed seven rungs to 27th place out of 70 economies in the IMD World Digital and AI Ranking (WDAIR) 2026 from 34th place last year, becoming the second-highest-ranked country in ASEAN after Singapore.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the achievement was driven particularly by a 21-place improvement in artificial intelligence (AI) adoption to 14th place globally, a 10-place improvement in efficiency to 28th place, and Malaysia’s implementation of the national AI strategy, which ranked 12th.
“Malaysia also ranks 18th in workforce development, second globally in graduates in sciences, fifth in venture capital, sixth in high-tech exports and eighth in investment incentives for AI.
“The Malaysia Digital Action Plan 2030 and the National AI Action Plan 2026-2030 (AI Nation 2030) aim to create up to 300,000 new AI-related jobs and contribute up to an additional 1.2 percentage points to gross domestic product (GDP) growth by 2030,” he said in a post on his official Facebook account today.
He added that under Budget 2027, RM30 million has been allocated through the Malaysia Digital Economy Corporation (MDEC) to help 4,000 micro, small and medium enterprises integrate AI and automate their operations.
The allocation will also support the training and certification of 5,000 AI professionals, as well as provide an additional 100,000 free AI subscriptions for youth.
The IMD WDAIR 2026 by the International Institute for Management Development (IMD) evaluates 70 economies based on 88 criteria across five key factors: governance, technology and infrastructure, efficiency, workforce Development, and values. — Bernama

Title: Stay away from 14 Hulu Selangor rivers, waterfalls amid water surge danger, Fire Dept warns; Pertak, Siling, Batang Kali top hotspots
Article:
HULU SELANGOR, Nov 11 — Fourteen recreational areas in Hulu Selangor have been identified as high-risk locations for water surges, with Sungai Pertak, Sungai Siling and Sungai Batang Kali emerging as the three main hotspots.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) Operations assistant director Ashrul Riezal Asbar said Sungai Batang Kali recorded four water surge incidents this year, followed by Sungai Siling with three and Sungai Pertak with two.
“Of the nine incidents recorded at these three locations, only the one at Sungai Pertak involved victims, while the others did not result in any casualties,” he told Bernama at the JBPM Forward Control Post at Jambatan Pertak here today.
He said the other 11 high-risk locations were Lata Medang in Kuala Kubu Bharu, Sungai Inki in Kalumpang, River View Sungai Bernam in Hulu Selangor, Sungai Sendat and Sungai Tua in Ulu Yam, Sungai Kedondong in Batang Kali, Sungai Cilin in Kuala Kubu Bharu, Sungai Pinang in Batang Kali, Air Terjun Serendah in Serendah, Air Terjun Semangkuk and Sungai Liam in Hulu Selangor.
In view of the north-east monsoon, Ashrul Riezal advised the public to temporarily suspend water-based recreational activities to avoid untoward incidents.
He said the advisory was aimed at raising awareness among local communities and visitors about the dangers of sudden water surges, particularly amid unpredictable weather conditions.
Eight people, comprising one Malaysian and seven foreigners, were swept away by strong currents during a water surge at Sungai Pertak at about 5.30pm last Monday.
Five were found drowned, including Malaysian V. Vijayan, 36, Nepalese national Kapali, 49, and Indian national B. Kunjanmalayil, 35. The identities of the other two, an Indian and a Sri Lankan, are being established.
The search continues for the remaining three victims, comprising two Indian nationals and a Yemeni. — Bernama

Title: IGP says Prisons Dept responsible for Najib’s home security
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — The Prisons Department is fully responsible for the security arrangements for former Prime Minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak, who has been serving the remainder of his jail sentence under house arrest at his residence in Langgak Duta here since yesterday.
Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM), as a law enforcement agency, maintained close cooperation with the Prisons Department to ensure compliance with the security requirements.
“Since the house (Najib’s residence) falls under the jurisdiction of the Sentul District Police Headquarters (IPD), I have instructed the IPD to conduct inspections and provide security monitoring from time to time,” he told reporters.
He was speaking after officiating at the 2026 PDRM Integrity Month celebration here today.
Mohd Khalid said PDRM had assigned several officers to assist the Prisons Department throughout the former prime minister’s period of serving the remainder of his sentence at home.
Yesterday, Najib began serving the remainder of his prison sentence in the SRC International Sdn Bhd case under house arrest after the High Court here ruled that the order should take effect immediately.
Judge Datuk Aslam Zainuddin made the decision after setting aside an order issued by the High Court Criminal Registry on November 6 against Najib, 73. — AFP

Title: Government steps in with RM15m monthly subsidy as palm oil costs rise
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — The government has approved a special incentive of about RM15 million a month under the Cooking Oil Price Control Mechanism (MKHMM) to maintain ceiling prices and ensure a stable supply of bottled pure palm cooking oil.
Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali said the decision, made at the Cabinet meeting on Nov 6, followed a surge in global crude palm oil (CPO) prices, which had significantly increased production costs for manufacturers.
“Through this mechanism, we can maintain the existing ceiling prices for 1kg, 2kg, 3kg and 5kg bottles, while providing special incentives to manufacturers producing bottled cooking oil,” he told a media conference held in conjunction with the 22nd Annual General Meeting of the Malaysian Muslim Restaurant Owners Association (PRESMA) here today.
He said based on the average global CPO price of RM4,400 per tonne in October 2026, the price of a 5kg bottle of cooking oil could have risen to RM34 without the intervention.
Under the mechanism, the ceiling prices of bottled pure palm cooking oil will remain at RM6.90 for 1kg, RM13.30 for 2kg, RM19.60 for 3kg and RM30.90 for 5kg, as stipulated under the Price Control and Anti-Profiteering Act 2011.
Armizan said the sustained increase in global CPO prices since June 2025 had placed mounting cost pressures on manufacturers, prompting some companies to halt production of bottled cooking oil.
He said the ministry (KPDN) had worked with the Finance Ministry and other relevant ministries to implement the mechanism as an intervention to ease cost-of-living pressures amid global market disruptions caused by the conflict in West Asia.
Meanwhile, PRESMA president Datuk Mohammed Mosin Abdul Razak said stable cooking oil prices would help restaurant operators better manage their business costs.
He also hoped the government would consider introducing targeted subsidies for restaurant operators in the future, similar to the assistance provided to manufacturers. — Bernama

Title: Car washer charged with murder over fatal Jalan Kuching crash that killed lorry driver
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — A car washer was brought before the Magistrate’s Court today on a charge of murdering a lorry driver in a fatal accident on Jalan Kuching here earlier this month.
Mohamad Imran Taj Maloor, 32, nodded in understanding after the charge was read out before Magistrate Faezahnoor Hassan.
No plea was recorded from the accused, as murder cases fall under the jurisdiction of the High Court.
He is accused of killing Indonesian lorry driver Yudi Hartono, 39, on Jalan Kuching heading from the city centre towards Segambut at 4.44am on November 4.
The charge is framed under Section 302 of the Penal Code, which carries the death penalty or imprisonment of up to 40 years and, where the death penalty is not imposed, not fewer than 12 strokes of the cane, upon conviction.
The prosecution was conducted by deputy public prosecutor Vivi Asnita Zaina’Larifin, while the accused was represented by lawyer Azleen Farahannis.
No bail was allowed, and the court set January 28 next year for mention.
Meanwhile, in a statement today, Kuala Lumpur Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department chief ACP Mohd Zamzuri Mohd Isa said that preliminary investigations found the car driven by the accused, with a 46-year-old male passenger, had struck the rear right side of the lorry.
“As a result of the collision, the lorry veered onto the left road shoulder while its driver, a 39-year-old Indonesian man, suffered severe injuries and was pronounced dead at the scene,” he said.
According to Mohd Zamzuri, an EBA II breath test recorded a blood alcohol reading of 61 mg/100ml for the car driver, while his passenger recorded 67 mg/100ml. — Bernama

Title: Azalina: Land acquisition must uphold rule of law, respect constitutional safeguards
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — Challenging decisions involving compulsory land acquisition is not an act of disloyalty but an essential part of upholding the rule of law, said Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said.
The Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) said that as Malaysia continued to pursue economic growth and modernise its infrastructure, compulsory land acquisition remained a necessary but sensitive public duty requiring transparency, procedural fairness and adequate compensation.
“From the perspective of democracy, challenging the exercise of power is not an act of disloyalty, rather it’s an essential part of the rule of law,” she said at the “Challenging Land Acquisition in Malaysia” book launch here today.
She said the pace of modern development must not outstrip governance standards and constitutional guarantees.
Azalina said the completion of major infrastructure projects, including railways, industrial hubs and highways, should not be the sole measure of success, as the government must also ensure that the institutions entrusted with such powers exercised them responsibly and in accordance with the law.
She said physical progress alone did not define a country’s stature, stressing that while buildings might transform a nation’s skyline, the rule of law defined its character.
Meanwhile, she commended the legal fraternity for publishing academic and practical works that enriched jurisprudence and provided guidance to future legal practitioners. — Bernama

Title: Nadma deploys 102,000 personnel ahead of 2026/2027 northeast monsoon
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — The National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) has mobilised nearly 102,000 personnel from various departments and agencies, along with 40,000 operational assets, in preparation for the 2026/2027 Northeast Monsoon (MTL).
Nadma Deputy Director of Operations Datuk Dr Abdul Gapar Abu Bakar said the preparations also included 8,321 temporary relief centres nationwide, with a combined capacity of up to 1.9 million flood victims.
“Among the assets prepared are around 2,450 boats and more than 3,000 four-wheel-drive vehicles and lorries, in addition to various other supporting assets.
“We have also prepared 170,000 ready-to-eat meals as initial food supplies for victims upon their arrival at relief centres, as well as 60,000 food kits containing essential items to be distributed to victims when they return to their homes,” he said.
He was speaking after appearing on Bernama Radio’s Fokus 30 programme, titled ‘Government Preparedness for the 2026/2027 Northeast Monsoon’, here today.
Commenting on ground-level operational coordination, Abdul Gapar said district officers are responsible for mobilising initial flood response by activating the District Disaster Operations Control Centre.
Meanwhile, the Incident Command Centre is headed by a Disaster Operations Commander, who is the district police chief, with the district Fire and Rescue Station chief serving as the deputy. The Malaysian Civil Defence Force will assist in coordinating rescue and evacuation operations.
“Apart from rescue agencies, Nadma also mobilises community leaders, non-governmental organisations (NGOs) and local communities through the Community-Based Disaster Risk Management (CBDRM) programme to support rescue operations and the management of relief centres,” he said.
At the same time, Abdul Gapar encouraged members of the public to download the Malaysia Disaster Information Management System (MyDIMS) application, launched by Nadma on April 24, to obtain disaster-related information.
He said the application sends notifications when users are within a 10-kilometre radius of a disaster-affected area. It also consolidates weather information, disaster updates and the locations of relief centres, including navigation guidance to these centres.
In addition, residents living in high-risk areas were reminded to keep emergency bags ready, containing important documents such as identity cards and passports, basic medication, food and drinking water supplies, as well as suitable clothing, in preparation for possible flooding. — Bernama

Title: Tragedy on the Melaka campaign trail: Car hits lorry, Alor Gajah PKR deputy chief dies in crash outside campaign operations room
Article:
JASIN, Nov 11 — An aide of the Pakatan Harapan (PH) candidate for the Asahan seat in the Melaka election was killed today when the car he was driving collided with a lorry, three days to voting day.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, who is also PH chairman, paid tribute to J. Samivel, 62, in a Facebook post today, noting that the deceased was also Alor Gajah PKR deputy division chief.
“I have received sad news from Melaka. Brother Samivel, the representative of the Harapan candidate for the Asahan state seat, was killed in a road accident this afternoon.
“As Alor Gajah Keadilan deputy division chief, Brother Samivel had long served and remained loyal to the struggle. May his service and spirit continue to guide our steps as we carry on this struggle.
“My thoughts and prayers, and Azizah’s, are with the late Samivel’s family and fellow comrades. May they be given strength and fortitude in facing this trying ordeal,” Anwar said, speaking also for his wife Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail.
The crash happened along Jalan Pondok Batang here at about noon, in front of PH’s main operations room for the Asahan seat, according to the New Straits Times.
Jasin district police chief Superintendent Lee Robert said police received information about the accident at about 12.45pm.
He said initial information showed that the car Samivel was in had collided with a lorry, which RTM reported was carrying fruit.
Lee said investigations were underway to determine the cause of the crash, and that more details would be released once police had the full picture.
Melaka Fire and Rescue Department public relations officer Mohd Hafidzatullah Rashid said the department received an emergency call at 12.22pm.
He said rescuers found Samivel trapped in the driver’s seat, and that he was pronounced dead by Health Ministry personnel before being handed over to police.
Samivel’s body was taken to the forensic unit of Jasin Hospital for a post-mortem, the NST reported.
The PH Election Department described his death as a great loss to his family, friends, party members and everyone who knew him, the NST reported.
It also thanked him for his service and contributions, particularly his hard work throughout the state election campaign.
Sinar Harian reported that Samivel was among the “backbones” of the campaign of PH’s Asahan candidate P. Denesh.
Denesh, who was on a walkabout and house visits in Kampung Jus Permai at the time, rushed to the scene, when he heard the news.
Denesh is the challenger against Asahan incumbent from Barisan Nasional, Datuk Dr Fairul Nizam Roslan.
